focus_questions.question: Is the cloud margin expansion durable, or is capitalised infrastructure flattering it?
focus_questions.where: 'Earnings Quality — Commentary' ("The live earnings-quality question is capitalisation, not accruals"), 'Historical Financial Analysis — Composition and earnings quality', 'Segment Analysis — Commentary', and the red-team item 'Red team — profitability, severity 3/5' in 'Validation & Disagreements'.
focus_questions.with_what_evidence: Mechanism is identified and sourced: capex $115.9bn against OCF $182.9bn; EBITDA $194.2bn vs operating income $155.2bn (so D&A ≈ $39bn); PP&E $313.1bn close to a year's revenue; 10-K narrative that Microsoft Cloud gross margin percentage fell on AI infrastructure investment, offset by Azure/M365 efficiency. The note then declares useful lives 'not quantified' and refuses to size the flattery. The red team points out that a depreciation_rate (0.196) and capex-to-depreciation (1.636) were computed but unused — though both are footnoted 'for FY2022', not FY2026. The five-year gross-margin series (69.8% FY24 → 67.9% FY26) and operating-margin series (42.1% → 46.8%) exist only in footnotes [^42]–[^56] to an unrendered chart; the body never confronts the question's premise with them, and the Executive Summary wrongly says 'no prior-period comparatives sit here'. Direction argued, magnitude absent.

focus_questions.question: How much of the AI capital expenditure is already earning a return, and what does the free cash flow trajectory look like if it does not?
focus_questions.where: 'Growth Outlook — What is not disclosed' and 'Scenarios & Sensitivities — Sensitivity Commentary' ("None of these swings can be sized without recorded scenario outputs, and we do not supply figures we cannot source").
focus_questions.with_what_evidence: The note explicitly declines both halves: 'Nothing before us isolates revenue from AI services... no dollar amount', remaining performance obligations 'not among the figures available', partner circularity 'quantify nothing'. No downside FCF path is given. The only FCF material is FY2026 OCF $182.9bn and capex $115.9bn (implying $67.0bn, never stated — 'a minority of the operating inflow') and an unexplained 'Free cash flow $139,225m' FCFF headline in 'At a glance' that does not tie to OCF − capex. DCF assumptions (capex intensity 20.3%, depreciation intensity 8.7%) exist in 'Forecast Assumptions' but no forecast FCF, EV or equity value is shown, so the reader cannot even see the base trajectory, let alone a no-return case.

focus_questions.question: What does the balance of revenue growth against operating leverage imply for the 12-month view?
focus_questions.where: 'Valuation — Discounted Cash Flow — Commentary' ("a flat margin assumption across the forecast is an aggressive one on this base, not a neutral one"), the 'Forecast Assumptions' table (revenue growth 13.7%, EBIT margin 44.2%), 'Growth Outlook — Base case', and the header line 'Non-binding view: no view reached'.
focus_questions.with_what_evidence: The direction of operating leverage is argued (margin fades as compute-heavy revenue mixes in; EBITDA–EBIT gap widening on depreciation) and the DCF implicitly encodes it (44.2% EBIT margin vs 46.8% FY2026 actual, with 13.7% growth). But the note never computes a revenue growth rate in text — FY2026 growth of 17.8% is derivable only from the 'Revenue history' table (281,724 → 331,839) — never states the share price, and offers no 12-month view of any kind; 'Catalysts' finds no dated event after 11 September 2026. The inputs are on the page; the answer is not.

verifiability.how_a_figure_is_checked: Every figure carries a footnote. Reported line items cite the SEC XBRL companyfacts JSON for CIK 0000789019 (URL given, published 29 July 2026, retrieved 11 September 2026, artefact hash f8aae2965b20): open the JSON, find the tag for FY2026 (e.g. Revenues, NetIncomeLoss, PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment) and compare. Ratios cite a formula, the inputs' names and a code version (f17f7158e569), so you redo the division from the cited line items. Narrative claims cite the 10-K or 8-K URL. The DCF per-share outputs cite only 'value per share = equity value / shares outstanding' with no EV, equity value or forecast FCF shown, so those cannot be re-performed from the note.
verifiability.figures_checked: Read-only brief, so internal arithmetic only. Ties: gross margin 225.5/331.8 = 67.96%; operating margin 155.2/331.8 = 46.8%; net margin 133.7/331.8 = 40.3%; net debt 40,294 − 20,935 = 19,359; current ratio 207,710/168,825 = 1.230; quick ratio (20,935 + 55,908 + 80,900)/168,825 = 0.934; debt/equity 40,294/442,387 = 0.091; equity weight 442,387/482,681 = 0.9165; WACC 0.0962 × 0.9165 + 0.0604 × 0.0835 = 0.0932; EPS $17.95 × 7,453m = $133.8bn vs net income $133.7bn. Does not tie: 'Free cash flow $139,225m' (FCFF formula) vs OCF − capex = $67.0bn, and the text never states either; DPS $0.91 vs dividends paid $26.4bn / 7,427m shares = $3.55; 'Value per share (base) $485.29' vs the section's own $242.78 and $449.79; the six red-team disagreements cite calculations footnoted 'for FY2022' ([^137]–[^141]) against FY2026 claims — the 0.4206/0.4177 operating margins it calls 'unreconciled' are the FY2022/FY2023 values in [^47]/[^48], so the severity-5/5 finding is a year mismatch, yet it was escalated unresolved.

The DCF's forecast FCF path, enterprise value and equity value, and what 'Value per share (base) $485.29' represents
rubric.first_thing_to_check: What 'Value per share (base) $485.29' in 'At a glance' actually is. It matches neither DCF output in the valuation section ($242.78 Gordon growth, $449.79 exit multiple), the Executive Summary says no per-share value exists on the record, the red team says the calculation index holds no DCF, and the note never states the current share price to compare any of them against. Until that headline is reconciled — and set against a price — nothing else in the note can be acted on. Second: confirm the six red-team disagreements are FY2022-vs-FY2026 mismatches, as the footnotes suggest, and not real errors in the FY2026 figures.
rubric.strongest_paragraph: 'Earnings Quality — Commentary', second paragraph: \"The live earnings-quality question is capitalisation, not accruals. Capital expenditure of $115.9 billion consumed the larger part of operating cash flow, and every dollar of that infrastructure spend returns to the income statement as depreciation over an assumed life. Reported operating margin is therefore as sensitive to depreciation-schedule assumptions as it is to pricing and mix.\" It names the exact mechanism behind focus question 1, anchors it to sourced FY2026 figures, and is honest about the missing input (useful lives) rather than inventing one. The 'Valuation — Commentary' paragraph on capex intensity ('holding intensity nearer recent levels for longer is the more defensible posture, and it lowers value per share') is the runner-up for the same reason.
rubric.weakest_paragraph: Executive Summary, 'Key Points', second bullet: \"Valuation support for the current price: the disclosure does not exist. No discounted cash flow, cost of equity, weighted average cost of capital, terminal value, value per share or peer multiple sits on this record.\" It is false within the same document — thirty lines above, 'At a glance' prints WACC 9.3% and value per share $485.29, and a full DCF section follows with two terminal methods and a 25-cell sensitivity grid. The thesis statement repeats the denial. A reader who trusts the summary and stops there is told the opposite of what the note contains. Close second: the 'Red team — profitability, severity 5/5' disagreement, whose 'unreconciled' figures are FY2022/FY2023 values compared against FY2026 claims, escalated without anyone noticing the year.
rubric.overall: As a data appendix on Microsoft's FY2026 consolidated accounts this is unusually well sourced: every line item points at the SEC XBRL feed with a hash, every ratio carries its formula, and the arithmetic ties on every figure I could re-perform by hand. The earnings-quality and valuation commentary correctly identify capitalisation policy and capex intensity as the swing variables, which is the right frame for the brief. As a research note answering the three focus questions it fails. It reaches no view, never states the share price, and its headline per-share value ($485.29) matches neither of its own DCF outputs while its executive summary insists no valuation exists — the sections read as if written in isolation and never reconciled (the Key Risks table even says operating cash flow is 'not among the figures available here', five sections after quoting it). Question 1 gets the mechanism but no magnitude; the five-year margin series that would test durability sits only in footnotes to a chart that is not rendered, while the body claims no comparatives exist. Question 2 is explicitly declined on both halves. Question 3 is never posed as a 12-month question. Segment figures, guidance, named competitors and a quantified bear case are all missing; the board changes and the IRS matter are unsourced; DPS is mislabelled; the 'free cash flow' headline does not tie to OCF minus capex. The six red-team disagreements, presented as unresolved and escalated, appear to compare FY2022 calculation records to FY2026 claims — which both undermines confidence in the process and leaves the reader unable to tell whether the FY2026 figures are disputed. For a private investor deciding whether to add to a position, this is 35 minutes to learn that FY2026 margins were high and capex was $115.9bn, with no price, no view and a contradictory valuation; a Claude session with the 10-K, the Q4 call transcript and the 2 September 8-K would answer the three questions more directly, though with weaker provenance than this note's footnotes provide.

focus_questions.question: Is the cloud margin expansion durable, or is capitalised infrastructure flattering it?
focus_questions.where: Earnings Quality > Commentary ('The live earnings-quality question is capitalisation, not accruals'); Segment Analysis > Commentary; Historical Financial Analysis > 'Composition and earnings quality'; Scenarios & Sensitivities > 'Bear case — shorter depreciation schedules'; Validation & Disagreements > 'Red team — profitability, severity 3/5'
focus_questions.with_what_evidence: The document frames the question correctly and then declines to answer it numerically. It states the 10-K attributes a decline in Microsoft Cloud gross margin percentage to AI infrastructure investment (so the premise of 'expansion' is actually contradicted at cloud level, while consolidated operating margin in footnotes [^47]-[^51] rose 42.1% to 46.8% FY2022-FY2026 — a series the body claims it does not have: 'no prior-period comparatives sit here'). It gives PP&E $313.1bn vs revenue $331.8bn, capex $115.9bn vs OCF $182.9bn, the EBITDA-EBIT gap of ~$39bn as depreciation, and says useful lives are 'unverifiable' and it 'does not estimate them'. The sharpest evidence — capex/depreciation of 1.636x and depreciation rate 0.196, i.e. the current charge reflects a much smaller asset base than the one being built — appears only in the red-team disagreement, unresolved, and footnoted to FY2022 calculations ([^140]). No quantification of how much depreciation policy flatters margin.

focus_questions.question: How much of the AI capital expenditure is already earning a return, and what does the free cash flow trajectory look like if it does not?
focus_questions.where: Growth Outlook > 'What is not disclosed' and 'What the numbers do support'; Cash Flow Analysis > Commentary; Valuation — Discounted Cash Flow > Commentary ('holding intensity nearer recent levels for longer... lowers value per share'); Scenarios & Sensitivities > Sensitivity Commentary ('None of these swings can be sized')
focus_questions.with_what_evidence: First half: explicitly not answerable on the evidence held — 'Nothing before us isolates revenue from AI services, AI-related cloud consumption or Copilot', remaining performance obligations not available, partner/investee circularity 'quantif[ies] nothing'. It offers ROIC 27.1% (NOPAT $125.1bn / invested capital $461.7bn, neither footnoted with a formula, and disputed by the red team at $72.4bn / $202.4bn) as the proxy. Second half: no FCF trajectory is modelled. The body defines FCF as OCF less capex but never states the ~$67bn result; the At-a-glance 'Free cash flow $139,225m' [^8] is an FCFF from the DCF with no period and does not reconcile with OCF minus capex. The DCF's capex intensity of 0.2026 (about $67bn on FY2026 revenue) sits far below actual FY2026 capex of $115.9bn (0.349 of revenue) with no explanation, and the commentary argues the opposite posture. Only the direction ('it lowers value per share') is given for the no-return case.

focus_questions.with_what_evidence: No 12-month view is offered, no target price, and no share price is quoted anywhere despite a daily price series being listed as a source. Revenue growth is derivable from the At-a-glance history ($281.7bn to $331.8bn, ~17.8%) but is never computed or discussed; operating margin history exists only in chart footnotes. The DCF assumes 13.7% growth and a 44.2% EBIT margin — a fade from 46.8%, i.e. negative operating leverage — without saying why. The only forward statement is 'growth from here [remains] cloud- and capacity-led, and durable for as long as returns on invested capital stay near the level recorded', which is a condition, not a view. No management guidance is cited.

rubric.first_thing_to_check: The At-a-glance 'Value per share (base) $485.29' [^11]: it equals the top of the football-field range [^102], matches neither the Gordon growth ($242.78) nor the exit-multiple ($449.79) result in the DCF section, and the DCF's capex intensity of 0.2026 implies roughly $67bn of capex on FY2026 revenue against an actual $115.9bn — while the executive summary and the red team both state that no valuation exists on the record. Establish which case produced $485.29, what capex path it assumes, and whether the DCF section is part of the approved record at all.
rubric.strongest_paragraph: Balance Sheet & Liquidity > Commentary, second paragraph: 'Funded leverage is light: short-term debt of $9.2 billion plus long-term debt of $31.1 billion gives total debt of $40.3 billion against equity of $442.4 billion... Two qualifications matter more than that headline.' It states a sourced ratio, immediately names what it omits ($16.5bn of lease liabilities, $316.0bn of total liabilities, rising finance-lease interest), and explains why the funded-debt figure is quoted anyway — a number, its limits, and the reason, all in one place.
rubric.weakest_paragraph: Executive Summary > Thesis: 'That is where this record's support ends: it holds no valuation output, no discount rate and no peer multiple, so we take no view on whether the 11 September 2026 share price is fair.' It is contradicted by the At a glance table three lines above (WACC 9.3%, value per share $485.29) and by an entire Discounted Cash Flow section further down; a reader cannot tell which half of the document to believe, and the Key Risks bullet that follows ('no prior-period comparatives sit here to test durability') is likewise contradicted by five years of margins in footnotes [^42]-[^56].
rubric.overall: This is a carefully footnoted single-year description of Microsoft's FY2026 accounts, not the research note the brief asked for. Its consolidated figures and simple ratios are internally consistent and traceable to SEC XBRL and the 10-K, and the balance-sheet, cash-flow and earnings-quality sections reason honestly about what a funded-debt ratio or an operating margin omits. But it reaches no view, quotes no share price, cites no guidance, names no competitor, gives no segment figures, and its bear case is explicitly unquantified. The valuation is the central failure: a DCF section with stated assumptions and two per-share outputs coexists with an executive summary and a red-team finding that say no valuation exists; the headline 'base' $485.29 matches neither output and sits at the top of the range; the DCF's capex intensity (0.20) is far below FY2026 actual (0.35) even as the commentary argues intensity should be held high; and a $139.2bn 'free cash flow' is unreconciled with OCF minus capex of $67bn. Six red-team disagreements, one at severity 5/5, are left 'escalated' with no resolution in the text, and their footnotes suggest FY2022 calculations were compared against FY2026 claims — something the document neither notices nor corrects. On the three focus questions it correctly identifies the disclosure gaps (useful lives, AI revenue, RPO) and ranks the sensitivities (capital intensity, margin persistence, terminal treatment, discount rate), which is the most useful content, but it converts none of that into a number, a scenario path or a 12-month implication.

rubric.first_thing_to_check: The 'At a glance' pair 'Value per share (base) $485.29' [^11] and 'Free cash flow $139,225m' [^8]: neither is reconciled to the body — the DCF section's own outputs are $242.78 (Gordon growth) and $449.79 (exit multiple), and operating cash flow less capex from the document's own figures is ~$67bn. Find which calculation and which period produced each; until then the headline table is unreliable. Immediately after, confirm that the six red-team disagreements are FY2022-vs-FY2026 period mismatches (their footnotes [^137]-[^141] all read 'for FY2022') and clear or uphold them, because as written the note carries an unresolved severity-5 challenge to every margin it uses.
rubric.strongest_paragraph: Balance Sheet & Liquidity — Commentary, second paragraph ('Funded leverage is light: short-term debt of $9.2 billion plus long-term debt of $31.1 billion gives total debt of $40.3 billion...'). Every figure ties to the adjoining Financial History table [^63], the arithmetic reproduces (40.3/442.4 = 0.09x; 40.3 − 20.9 = 19.4), and it immediately qualifies its own headline with lease liabilities of $16.5bn, rising finance-lease interest and total liabilities of $316.0bn — 'quoted here for comparability, not as the whole obligation picture'.
rubric.weakest_paragraph: Executive Summary — Key Points, second bullet ('Valuation support for the current price: the disclosure does not exist. No discounted cash flow, cost of equity, weighted average cost of capital, terminal value, value per share or peer multiple sits on this record'). It is contradicted on the same page by the 'At a glance' table (WACC 9.3%, value per share $485.29) and by the full Valuation — Discounted Cash Flow section; the Investment Thesis repeats the denial. A reader cannot tell which half of the note to believe.
rubric.overall: The note has strong plumbing and a hollow centre. Reported figures trace to the SEC XBRL feed and the 10-K/8-K URLs with artefact hashes, calculated ratios carry formulas and a code version, and the internal arithmetic on leverage, liquidity and margins reproduces. But it does not answer the brief. It states no view ('no view reached'), shows no share price, and never engages the 12-month horizon. The three focus questions are mostly declared unanswerable — even where the cited 10-K contains the data (segment dollars, useful lives, remaining performance obligations) — and the five-year margin series that would have addressed durability and operating leverage sits unused in chart footnotes while the text claims no comparatives exist. Internal contradictions undercut what is there: the Executive Summary denies any valuation exists while a DCF is presented; the headline 'base' value of $485.29 matches neither terminal method ($242.78 / $449.79); the headline free cash flow of $139.2bn contradicts the body's own OCF-less-capex residual of ~$67bn; dividends per share of $0.91 is a quarterly rate; and the six red-team disagreements, all of which cite FY2022 calculations against FY2026 claims, are left 'Escalated' rather than resolved. No competitor is named, no guidance is given, board changes are unsourced, the bear case has no number, and the peer analysis produced nothing. Useful as a sourced fact sheet on FY2026 consolidated accounts; not usable as a research note for a 12-month decision.

rubric.first_thing_to_check: The FY26 depreciation and amortisation charge. Open the FY26 10-K [S2] cash flow statement and read the full-year 'Depreciation, amortization, and other' line, then re-run §8's magnitude check: the note's printed formula '155.237 - (115.95 - 44.1)' yields ~$83bn (~25% margin), not the '$63bn' / '19%' it states, and the $24bn low end of its $24-44bn range comes from an accumulated-depreciation delta that ignores asset retirements. The '$72-92bn per year of economic cost not yet in the P&L' claim, §15 risk 6 and the answer to focus question 1's second half all rest on this range.
rubric.strongest_paragraph: §4 'Intelligent Cloud — growing fast, earning less per dollar' together with the §8 decomposition table ('Gross margin % change -88bp / Opex-revenue change +204bp / Net +116bp'). Every input is a specific row of one SEC exhibit [S5], the arithmetic re-performs exactly, the segment tables tie to group totals, and it directly overturns the premise of focus question 1 with filed numbers rather than commentary.
rubric.weakest_paragraph: §8 'Yes, capitalisation is flattering the reported margin — and here is the arithmetic.' The depreciation figure is not read from any filing but bracketed between two proxies (a Q4 'D&A and other non-cash' line from stock-analysis-on.net annualised x4, and a nine-month accumulated-depreciation delta that omits retirements), giving a $24-44bn range so wide that the resulting '$72-92bn deferral' is not a finding; and the printed magnitude-check formula does not produce its own stated result ($63bn / 19%). Runner-up: §9 'Balance Sheet & Liquidity', where the 30 June 2026 column is from Yahoo and a Beancount blog and the finance-lease figure is admittedly irreconcilable ($62bn vs $16.53bn).
rubric.overall: A serious, unusually candid note whose FY26 income-statement and segment work is primary-sourced (EDGAR 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K segment exhibit, IR pages), internally reconciled (§18.1) and arithmetically sound on re-performance, and whose DCF is fully transparent with the two decisive assumptions (ERP 5.0%, beta 1.00) honestly labelled as unsourced. The Underweight/$405 view is argued from the 1.84% FCF yield against a 4.95% risk-free rate and a 420bp Intelligent Cloud gross-margin decline, not recited, and a numbered bear case ($186) sits in the body. The reservations are substantive. First, the note appears written to a different question set than the brief: focus question 1 is answered squarely, but question 2 is answered as 'how much revenue is AI' (no return-on-capex measure of any kind, no bear-case FCF path — only FY36 endpoints), and question 3's ingredients (decelerating growth, exhausted opex leverage, 45.1% exit margin, FY27E EPS +7%) are never synthesised into a 12-month statement; the note itself says the disagreement with the market is about the discount rate, not the trajectory. Second, the capitalisation argument that carries question 1's second half rests on a derived $24-44bn depreciation range and contains an arithmetic error ($63bn stated where the printed formula gives $83bn), even though the 10-K it cites contains the actual line. Third, sourcing quality degrades sharply away from the income statement: the balance sheet, lease obligations ($329.1bn from btw.media/Substack), FY27 guidance (LicenseQ blog), and all 90-day news (CNN/CNBC quote pages 'accessed 11 Sep') are secondary or dynamic and would not reproduce on a later check. Fourth, checklist gaps: no company-named 10-K risk factors, no management/board changes, no acquisitions, no regulatory matters, and a comps table the author calls 'unbuilt'. Fifth, the target is set at an 8.87% WACC the author does not centrally endorse, which blurs the recommendation. Actionable as a well-constructed sceptical frame on cash conversion and capital intensity, provided the reader pulls FY26 D&A, the as-filed balance sheet and lease note, and the primary guidance before relying on §8, §9 or §12.

Nearly every number traces to an SEC or RNS URL and my re-computation of ~25 figures found only two trivial slips. rubric.first_thing_to_check: Whether an 8.5% cost of equity is defensible: pull a current 10-year Treasury yield and a beta for AZN and run CAPM. The note states in Section 18 that 'the rating is one assumption deep' and that at 7.2% 'the stock is fairly valued and the rating should be Hold'; the 13.3 construction is an assumption layered on the company's 4.9% bond coupons, not a derivation, so this single check can flip the conclusion. Immediately after that, open the Patent Expiries PDF (source #21) to see what actually falls due inside the horizon, because the brief's first question is answered only from already-begun erosion.
rubric.strongest_paragraph: Section 1, the paragraph beginning 'The disagreement between my DCF and the multiple is identifiable and is the crux of this note.' It states the whole argument in one place with sourced numbers: 15.7x FY2026E and 16.4x TTM Core EPS is not demanding, but Core EPS excludes 'the amortisation of intangibles, impairments, legal settlements and restructuring charges' (quoted from the H1 2026 6-K) while the cash cost of buying that IP recurs in investing cash flow — a $4,735m gap at the operating line in FY2025 computed from the results presentation. Everything from Section 10's three-definition owner-cash-flow table to the reverse DCF follows from this paragraph, and a reader can check every input in it.
rubric.weakest_paragraph: Section 12, 'The patent-cliff question (part 2 of 3 posed in the brief)', the 'Method note': 'I was unable to extract the per-product expiry years from that document within my research budget, and I therefore do not state any product's expiry date.' For a brief whose first question is exposure to expiries falling due inside the horizon, this concedes the load-bearing fact, and the appendix nevertheless lists the same PDF under 'Every source below was retrieved and read'. The substitute answer (a global Farxiga figure for a US event, and run-rate declines in two therapy areas) measures erosion already under way, not what falls due next. Close runner-up: Section 9's use of Dukascopy for working capital, current ratio and interest cover after Section 18 item 8 shows the same source's market cap and EV to be wrong.
rubric.overall: A serious, transparent and internally consistent note: the view (Underweight, $132) is stated on the first page, argued from a sourced Core-versus-cash mechanism rather than recited, tested with a reverse DCF, three explicit scenarios and two sensitivity grids, and every computed figure reproduces from its stated inputs. Sourcing discipline is unusually good — primary filings are linked, secondary sources are labelled and several are discarded with reasons, and the author lists what was not read. The reservations are substantial. First, the note answered a different brief: its own 'part 1' is US drug pricing and 'part 3' is whether oncology is 'in the price', so this brief's Q2 (approvals versus assumptions) and Q3 (dividend plus R&D through the horizon) are answered only by inference across Sections 4, 9–13, and Q1 is answered from already-crystallised LOEs because the expiry schedule was not read. Second, four admitted gaps sit exactly where the brief needs evidence: no patent dates, no US pricing primary source, no governance or board changes, no peer multiples. Third, checklist items 4 and 6 are absent, and balance-sheet ratios lean on a secondary site the note elsewhere distrusts. Fourth, the document has production defects — stray non-document text fused into the title line, and an appendix cut off mid-row at source #40. The author's own verdict is the right one: the rating is one assumption (cost of equity) deep. Usable as a well-built starting point; not yet a note to act on for this brief's questions.

rubric.first_thing_to_check: Open the 20-F consolidated income statement and confirm FY2025 revenue $58,739m, gross profit $48,106m and operating profit $13,743m. The document prints, unresolved, a severity-5 red-team finding that "Every headline margin in the draft is contradicted by the recorded calculations"; the footnotes to those findings ([^107]-[^110], [^113]) say "for FY2021"/"for FY2022", suggesting a period mismatch rather than a real error, but the body never reconciles it. If the three FY2025 lines hold, every ratio in the note stands and the escalations are noise; if they do not, nothing in the note can be used.
rubric.strongest_paragraph: "Historical Financial Analysis" → "Returns on capital" paragraph: "Return on equity is 21.0% and return on invested capital 15.6%, the latter built from NOPAT of $11,339m over invested capital of $72,578m. The construction matters and is stated plainly rather than assumed..." — it defines its own number, says what a stricter capital definition would do to it, and limits the conclusion to what a single year can support.
rubric.weakest_paragraph: "Executive Summary" → "Key Points", the bullets "Growth is unevidenced: ... with no prior-year comparatives no growth rate is asserted and none should be inferred" and "No invested-capital, cost-of-capital or return-on-invested-capital figure is on record". Both are contradicted by the document itself: the "Revenue history" table two inches above gives FY2021-FY2025 revenue ($37,417m to $58,739m, an 8.6% FY2025 rise the reader must compute), footnotes [^55]-[^69] hold five years of margins, and the Investment Thesis quotes ROIC of 15.6%.
rubric.overall: A candid but hollow note. What it does well: the FY2025 headline accounts are sourced to the SEC XBRL feed and the 20-F, every ratio carries its formula and code version, and the arithmetic reconciles. What it fails: none of the three focus questions is answered — no product is named, no expiry date given, no guidance quoted, no H1 2026 results, no valuation, no share price, no view. The document contradicts itself (five-year revenue history at the top versus "no prior-year comparatives" in the summary; "no ROIC on record" in the summary versus ROIC 15.6% in the thesis), and prints nine unresolved red-team escalations — several apparently comparing FY2025 claims to FY2021/22 register entries — without telling the reader which way to read them. Business Overview and Segment Analysis assert that no therapy-area or product revenue split exists when AstraZeneca's annual report contains one; the document simply did not reach it. A private investor gets a verified snapshot of the December 2025 balance sheet and income statement, and a list of things to look up elsewhere, dressed as a research note. Not actionable on its own.

focus_questions.question: How exposed is revenue to the patent expiries falling due inside the horizon?
focus_questions.where: "Segment Analysis → Commentary"; "Investment Thesis → Supporting Pillars" (bull proposition row); "Key Risks → Commentary"
focus_questions.with_what_evidence: No evidence at all, and the note says so four times. Segment Analysis: "the underlying patent expiry dates, US regulatory exclusivity periods, and ex-US supplementary protection certificate or data-exclusivity dates for individual products were not present in the material reviewed for this section, so no product-by-product exclusivity mapping can be offered here". It also refuses to proxy the exposure, and explains why: apportioning worldwide product revenue by a group-level regional ratio "would manufacture a figure not actually reported and is avoided here". Not one AstraZeneca product is named anywhere in the document as facing expiry; no expiry date, no exposed revenue line, no erosion rate, no biosimilar filing. The bull pillar concedes it: "No product-level or patent-expiry detail sits in the evidence before us, so the proposition is stated, not settled." The refusal is principled and I would rather have it than a fabricated number, but the brief's first question comes back blank.

focus_questions.question: Is the oncology pipeline's contribution to growth sourced from approvals and launches, or from assumptions about them?
focus_questions.where: "Growth Outlook → What is not evidenced"; "Scenarios & Sensitivities → Base case"; "Catalysts"; "Validation & Disagreements" (Red team — growth, severity 3/5)
focus_questions.with_what_evidence: The meta-answer is given plainly and it is "assumptions": "Asset-level late-stage disclosure — indication, phase, registry record and first plausible revenue period for each registrational programme — is not available in the material underlying this section, and no management revenue ambition can be quoted verbatim", and the base case "assumes in-horizon readouts and approvals deliver at historical rates ... so the assumption is a judgement, not a disclosure". Two real approval/readout events are sourced to SEC-filed releases of 8 September 2026 (Etcamah in HR+ breast cancer [^17]; Imfinzi+Imdelltra overall survival in small cell lung cancer [^111]), but nothing is drawn from them beyond the observation that HR+ is "the most common subtype of breast cancer" and that "its commercial effect is not quantified in any recorded figure". Oncology's contribution to growth is never sized in dollars or percentage points. The note's own red team then undercuts even the qualitative claim: the inference that the growth debate "now centres on late-stage oncology" rests only on "the recency of two regulatory releases dated 8 September 2026", and "Recency of a press release is not evidence of revenue weight." Catalysts is empty by policy — "no announced FDA or EMA decision dates, advisory-committee dates, congress presentation slots" — so there is no forward pipeline calendar either.

focus_questions.question: Does the balance sheet support the dividend and the R&D commitment together through the horizon?
focus_questions.where: "Cash Flow Analysis → Commentary"; "Capital Allocation → Commentary"; "Balance Sheet & Liquidity → Commentary"; "Growth Outlook → Capacity to fund it"
focus_questions.with_what_evidence: The best-served of the three questions, and the only one with real numbers behind it. FY2025 operating cash flow of $14,575m [^84], dividends paid $4,971m [^85], R&D $14,232m [^38], net debt $23,911m at 1.27x EBITDA [^88], interest cover 8.1x [^89], current ratio 0.94 [^80], debt repayments $2,029m against proceeds of $15m [^83], and the statement that "no share repurchases have been made since 2012". The Balance Sheet section refuses the easy conclusion: "on the stricter conventions coverage reads as adequate rather than comfortable", and it names the conventions (capitalised lease liabilities of $1.4bn, pension obligations, gross finance expense) that would show "leverage appreciably higher and coverage appreciably thinner". But the addition the question actually asks for is never performed: dividends of $4,971m plus R&D of $14,232m is $19,203m against $14,575m of operating cash flow, and the note never puts the two commitments side by side against the cash line. There is no capex figure ("there is no separate capital expenditure line"), so no free cash flow, so no coverage ratio for the two commitments together. And "through the horizon" is not addressed at all — the balance sheet on record closes 31 December 2025, a EUR2.55bn bond was admitted to trading on 1 September 2026 [^19] whose effect is "unquantifiable here", and the leverage and coverage figures that carry the answer are exactly the ones the note's own severity-5 red-team entry disputes (claimed 1.27x and 8.1x against recorded 3.22x/2.50x and 0.81x/2.79x).

Group figures stand in. Worse for a reader of the file: the "Segment mix" heading carries a line of eighteen footnote markers [^20]–[^37], every one of them the identical 20-F URL, then "*Rendered in the HTML and PDF editions of this report.*" — a promised chart that is not in this document, sourced eighteen times over to a filing whose brand-level detail the same section says appears only in "supplementary geographic disclosures incorporated by reference".

verifiability.how_a_figure_is_checked: Two routes, one excellent and one that dead-ends. Derived figures: every ratio carries a footnote giving the formula in words, the computed value to four decimals, the period, the code module and a code version hash — e.g. [^80] "current ratio = current assets / current liabilities = 0.9381 ... (aer.calc.ratios:current_ratio, code version 6d9c6c80d78a)". Both inputs are then printed in the "Balance Sheet & Liquidity → Financial History" table (28,723 and 30,617), so the check is one division inside the document, with no need to leave it. I re-derived a dozen this way and they all reconcile: 48,106/58,739 = 81.90%; 13,743/58,739 = 23.40%; 10,225/58,739 = 17.41%; 23,911/18,829 = 1.2699; 13,743/1,694 = 8.113; 11,339/72,578 = 15.62%; and net debt plus cash over implied equity gives 0.609 against the 0.6087 quoted. Base facts: every one traces to a single URL, the SEC XBRL companyfacts JSON for CIK 0000901832, with publisher, publication date, retrieval date, tier and an artefact hash in the Sources table. But the footnote names no XBRL tag, no context and no line reference, so finding "gross profit 48,106" inside a multi-megabyte JSON is real work and the note's own red team says some tags disagree with the text (filed operating cash flow $18,736m against the claimed $14,575m; AccountingProfit $12,402m against net income $10,225m) — a conflict I cannot adjudicate from this file. The 20-F footnote [^103] gives a working URL but no page, section or exhibit, and the governance and segment material is said to live in a companion "Annual Report and Form 20-F Information 2025" that is not in the Sources table. The price footnote [^114] prints its URL with api_token=REDACTED, so it cannot be re-fetched as written. And several figures carry no footnote at all: "basic earnings of $6.60 per share", R&D of "$3.5bn in the second quarter alone", "goodwill of $21.2bn", cash of "$7,058m at 30 June 2025", "single-A long-term ratings from both Moody's and Standard & Poor's", "committed bank facilities carrying no financial covenants", and the entire Capital Allocation figures table.
verifiability.figures_checked: Operating margin 23.4% ("Historical Financial Analysis → Figures", [^44]) — checked in under a minute: the footnote gives operating income / revenue, and both are in the Financial History table directly above (13,743 and 58,739), giving 0.2340. Net debt / EBITDA 1.27x ("Balance Sheet & Liquidity → Figures", [^77]) — also under a minute: 23,911 [^41] over 18,829 [^39] is 1.2699, and the EBITDA footnote itself explains its construction as operating income plus depreciation and amortisation, so I can see the 5,086 of D&A implied and judge it plausible. Operating cash flow $14,575m ("Cash Flow Analysis → Figures", [^84]) — not checkable from the document: it is a filed fact, the footnote points only at the companyfacts JSON with no tag named, and the note's own Validation section asserts the filed figure is $18,736m. The first two took two minutes between them; the third consumed the rest and ended unresolved.

still_to_look_up: Whether the recorded calculations quoted in the nine red-team disagreements are FY2021/FY2022 values rather than FY2025 ones. The footnotes attached to those entries say so on their face — [^107] is net debt to EBITDA 3.2233 for FY2021, [^110] is gross margin 0.6676 for FY2021, [^109] is ROIC 0.0823 for FY2022, [^113] is cash conversion 53.2411 for FY2021 — and the gross-margin series in [^55]–[^59] runs 0.6676, 0.7206, 0.8195, 0.8112, 0.819 across FY2021-FY2025, which places the disputed 81.9% squarely in the register for FY2025. If that reading is right, the document's entire adversarial review is period-mismatched and should never have reached print; if it is wrong, every margin, return and leverage figure in the note is unevidenced. Nothing in the file settles it.

The share count. Diluted EPS of $6.54 [^3] over net income of $10,225m [^2] implies about 1,563 million shares; the Valuation section says the filings carry no share count at all. One of the two statements is wrong, and with a share count there is no reason for the note to have no per-share valuation.

AstraZeneca's H1 2026 and Q1 2026 results. The note's latest interim is Q2 2025 and its annual accounts close 31 December 2025 — it concedes it is "several quarters behind this note's September 2026 as-of date". Two reporting cycles are missing at the as-of date, which is where any answer on patent-expiry erosion and on oncology launch revenue would actually live.

The product-level revenue table and the patent/exclusivity schedule — the 20-F therapy-area review and revenue note the bull pillar names as its "arbiter", plus Orange Book and SPC/data-exclusivity dates. Without them focus question 1 is unanswerable and the central proposition of the thesis is untestable.

The "Annual Report and Form 20-F Information 2025" companion document, for board composition, directors' tenure, remuneration policy and say-on-pay — the whole Management & Governance section points at it and it is not among the sources.

Capital expenditure, and the split of the $6,808m investing outflow between capex, acquisitions and portfolio transactions. Without it there is no free cash flow, and the dividend-plus-R&D coverage question cannot be closed.

What the two 8 September 2026 releases actually say in commercial terms — indication, line of therapy, competing agents, addressable population — since the document extracts only that HR+ is the most common breast cancer subtype.
Named peers and their multiples. Eight candidates were proposed and all eight excluded for want of filings and price series; they are not even listed, so there is no relative anchor of any kind.
The EUR2.55bn bond admitted to trading on 1 September 2026 — coupon, tenor, use of proceeds — and its effect on the post-year-end net debt and interest cost that the leverage answer turns on.
rubric.first_thing_to_check: The severity-5 profitability disagreement in \"Validation & Disagreements\". It states flatly that \"Every headline margin in the draft is contradicted by the recorded calculations\" — gross margin 0.668 and 0.721 against the claimed 81.9%, operating margin 0.028 and 0.085 against 23.4%, net margin 0.003 and 0.074 against 17.4% — and that \"No calculation in the index reproduces the claimed values\", escalated and never resolved. Check it first because it is cheap and because everything else hangs on it: its own footnote [^110] identifies the 0.6676 gross margin as FY2021, and the margin series in [^55]-[^59] shows 81.9% as the FY2025 figure, which suggests the red team is comparing FY2025 claims against FY2021/FY2022 calculations. Establish that and the document's arithmetic stands up (I re-derived a dozen ratios from the printed inputs and they all reconcile); fail to establish it and every margin, return and leverage figure here is unusable, which takes the one focus question the note does partly answer with it.
rubric.strongest_paragraph: \"Historical Financial Analysis → Commentary\", the \"Returns on capital\" paragraph. It quotes ROIC of 15.6% and then immediately tells the reader how it was built and how to distrust it: \"NOPAT is the year's operating result taxed at the effective rate implied by the tax charge; the denominators are closing balance-sheet amounts, not opening-and-closing averages. A definition that averaged the capital base, or that pulled more of the acquired intangible and goodwill stock into invested capital, would yield a lower return on the same profit\", and so \"A reader working on that stricter basis should treat the quoted return as the upper end of a range.\" It then declines the conclusion the number invites: \"On a single year, we do not claim that reinvestment has demonstrably cleared a cost of capital; we claim only that on this construction it sits above a plausible one, and that the judgement would reverse under a materially wider capital definition.\" That is a figure I can actually use, because I have been told what would move it and in which direction. The Balance Sheet leverage paragraph does the same job for net debt and interest cover, naming leases of $1.4bn and pension obligations as the conventions that would make coverage \"adequate rather than comfortable\".
rubric.weakest_paragraph: \"Valuation — Discounted Cash Flow → How These Figures Were Produced\". The entire section is: \"No discounted cash flow was produced, so there is no method to describe. The valuation needs a share count for the year ending 31 December 2025 and the filings carry none — neither diluted, basic nor a plain outstanding figure. Without one there is no per-share value to report, and an enterprise value on its own is not a recommendation.\" The brief asked for a valuation, and the stated reason for its absence is contradicted three times inside the same file: the At-a-glance table reports diluted EPS of $6.54 [^3] alongside net income of $10,225m [^2] from the same XBRL source, which implies a share count by division; Growth Outlook quotes \"basic earnings of $6.60 per share\"; and the Sources table carries a licensed daily price series for AZN to the as-of date [^114]. A note that has EPS, net income and a price series but reports no multiple, no price and no per-share value has not run out of inputs. The second weakest is \"Capital Allocation → Figures\", the only figures table in the document with no footnotes at all, whose commentary asserts that investing and financing \"together exceeding operating cash generation for the year\" when the printed numbers sum to $14,352m against $14,575m.
rubric.overall:
As a document handed to me cold, this is two things at once: unusually honest and unusually unusable.

What works. The audit trail is better than most sell-side notes I have read. Every derived figure carries its formula, its inputs, its value to four decimals, the code module that produced it and a version hash; every fact carries a publisher, a publication date, a retrieval date, a source tier and a URL, with artefact hashes in the Sources table. I could re-derive roughly a dozen ratios from numbers printed elsewhere in the same document and they all reconciled, including the non-obvious cross-check that net debt plus cash over implied equity reproduces the quoted 0.61 debt-to-equity. The prose is also disciplined about its own limits in ways that are analytically real rather than defensive: the refusal to apportion worldwide product revenue by a group-level regional ratio because it "would manufacture a figure not actually reported"; the refusal to decompose gross margin into price, volume and mix because "Any pricing-margin analysis built on these disclosures would be assumption dressed as measurement, and we decline to offer one"; the insistence that the gross-to-operating gap, not unit cost, is where the economics sit. Bear reasoning is in the body, not exiled to an appendix, and "What Would Change The View" names four falsifiers.

What does not. On the brief, it scores roughly zero, one and two. Patent-expiry exposure — the first focus question — is not addressed at all: no product is named, no expiry date given, no exposed revenue quantified, and the note says four times that the material was not available. Oncology's growth contribution gets an honest meta-answer (it is assumptions, not sourced approvals) but never a number, and Catalysts is empty. The dividend-and-R&D question is genuinely served with figures, yet the note never performs the addition the question asks for: $4,971m of dividends plus $14,232m of R&D against $14,575m of operating cash flow, with no capex line and therefore no free cash flow. On the checklist, four of ten items are absent, two are present but unsourced as presented, and four are sourced. No competitor is named anywhere. No director is named anywhere. There is no valuation, no price, no per-share figure, no peer multiple — and the reason offered for the missing valuation collapses against the document's own diluted EPS and licensed price series.

The deeper problem is that the note argues with itself and never resolves it. The header says "Non-binding view: no view reached"; the Investment Thesis says "Our central view is that...". The Executive Summary says "no invested-capital, cost-of-capital or return-on-invested-capital figure is on record" and "no prior-period comparatives" exist, while the Revenue history table shows FY2021-FY2025 and two later sections quote ROIC of 15.6% on invested capital of $72,578m. Cash Flow calls the year "the structural signature of a self-funding cash cycle"; Capital Allocation, on the same numbers, says the outflows "together exceed" operating cash flow, which they do not. And the "Validation & Disagreements" section publishes nine red-team challenges, two at severity 5/5, asserting that the headline margins, returns, leverage and cash conversion are all unevidenced — every one "Escalated for human decision at approval", every one still sitting here unresolved in the delivered document. Trace their footnotes and they look period-mismatched (FY2021 and FY2022 calculations held up against FY2025 claims), which would exonerate the numbers and indict the review; but the document does not say so, and a reader should not have to run that diagnosis to know whether the report's own margins are real.

Add that the financial base closes 31 December 2025 with Q2 2025 as the latest interim — two reporting cycles stale at a September 2026 as-of date, as the note itself concedes — and this reads as an auditable skeleton of a research note rather than a research note. I would trust an individual derived number in it more readily than in most notes, and I would not act on a single one of its conclusions.

focus_questions.question: How exposed is revenue to the patent expiries falling due inside the horizon?
focus_questions.where: "## Segment Analysis" → Commentary; "## Investment Thesis" → Supporting Pillars, row "Bull proposition: launches replace exclusivity losses inside the horizon"; "## Key Risks" → Commentary
focus_questions.with_what_evidence: None. The note states the gap rather than filling it: "the underlying patent expiry dates, US regulatory exclusivity periods, and ex-US supplementary protection certificate or data-exclusivity dates for individual products were not present in the material reviewed for this section", and "No product-level or patent-expiry detail sits in the evidence before us, so the proposition is stated, not settled". Not one medicine is named, no expiry date is given, no exposed revenue is sized, and the Key Risks commentary repeats that it "does not itemise product-level exclusivity dates, biosimilar filing dockets". It also refuses a proxy ("apportioning worldwide product revenue by a group-level regional ratio would manufacture a figure not actually reported") — honest, but the reader ends with zero exposure estimate. The disclosure is available in the very 20-F the note cites (revenue note, therapy-area review, IP section), so this is a sourcing failure, not an information vacuum.

focus_questions.question: Is the oncology pipeline's contribution to growth sourced from approvals and launches, or from assumptions about them?
focus_questions.where: "## Growth Outlook" → "**What is not evidenced:**" and "**Base case:**"; "## Scenarios & Sensitivities" → "**Base case:**"; footnotes [^17] (Etcamah HR+ breast cancer approval, 8 Sep 2026) and [^111] (Imfinzi+Imdelltra OS in small cell lung, 8 Sep 2026); "## Validation & Disagreements" → "Red team — growth, severity 3/5"
focus_questions.with_what_evidence: The meta-answer is given and is correct — it is assumptions: "Asset-level late-stage disclosure — indication, phase, registry record and first plausible revenue period for each registrational programme — is not available", "no management revenue ambition can be quoted verbatim", and the base case "assumes in-horizon readouts and approvals deliver at historical rates... the assumption is a judgement, not a disclosure". Two genuine T1 approval/readout filings dated 8 September 2026 are cited, and the note concedes their "commercial effect is not quantified in any recorded figure"; its own red team adds "Recency of a press release is not evidence of revenue weight." But nothing is quantified on either side: no oncology revenue line, no launch sales, no peak-sales or probability-of-success figure, no split of FY2025 revenue by therapy area. The "reinvestment engine" argument substitutes total R&D of $14.2bn for pipeline evidence — spend is an input, not a contribution to growth. Internally inconsistent too: the Executive Summary mentions the HR+ approval without naming the product, describing only that HR+ is "the most common subtype of breast cancer".

focus_questions.question: Does the balance sheet support the dividend and the R&D commitment together through the horizon?
focus_questions.where: "## Cash Flow Analysis" → Financial History table and "Uses."; "## Balance Sheet & Liquidity" → Commentary; "## Capital Allocation" → Commentary and Figures; "## Growth Outlook" → "**Capacity to fund it:**"; "## Validation & Disagreements" → "Red team — balance sheet, severity 5/5"
focus_questions.with_what_evidence: The best-served question. FY2025 operating cash flow $14,575m against dividends paid $4,971m and R&D of $14,232m (already expensed inside that operating cash line), financing outflow $7,544m of which debt repayments $2,029m versus proceeds $15m, net debt $23,911m at 1.27x EBITDA, interest cover 8.1x, current ratio 0.94, quick ratio 0.68, "committed bank facilities carrying no financial covenants alongside single-A long-term ratings", and "no share repurchases have been made since 2012" — dividend cover from operating cash is demonstrable on these figures. What is missing is most of the forward half: no capex line ("there is no separate capital expenditure line, no working capital detail, no share repurchase line"), so "Free cash flow... cannot be quantified"; no forward dividend or R&D commitment for the horizon, so "through the horizon" is asserted from a single closing balance sheet; the September 2026 EUR2.55bn bond is noted but never brought into the leverage figures ("their effect is unquantifiable here"); and the conclusion is contested by the note's own severity-5 red-team entry claiming net debt/EBITDA of 3.22x and interest cover of 0.81x, escalated and unresolved. The Capital Allocation section also mis-states its own arithmetic (see weakest_paragraph) and carries no citations at all.

checklist.item: segment revenue breakdown for the latest fiscal year
checklist.where: "## Segment Analysis" → "### Segment mix": a heading, eighteen footnotes all pointing at the same 20-F URL ([^20]–[^37]), and the line "*Rendered in the HTML and PDF editions of this report.*" — no numbers in this edition. Commentary says "AstraZeneca discloses only a single reportable operating segment" and "no segment-level revenue mix can be presented here". No therapy-area, product or geographic split appears anywhere, though the note itself says "Detailed brand-level sales appear only in supplementary geographic disclosures incorporated by reference into the filing" — i.e. it knew where to look and did not go.

checklist.item: management guidance or outlook for the coming period
checklist.where: "## Growth Outlook" → "**What is not evidenced:**" ("no management revenue ambition can be quoted verbatim") and "## Scenarios & Sensitivities" → "**What the evidence supports:**" (the material "does not... carry company guidance"). No revenue, EPS or margin guidance figure appears; the "Base case" is explicitly "a judgement drawn from financial structure alone; it is not a forecast anchored to named pipeline assets". Also no 2026 interim results at all — the latest interim on record is Q2 2025, which the note flags at "### Key Points" ("several quarters behind this note's September 2026 as-of date").

checklist.item: developments in the 90 days before the as-of date (results, deals, litigation, product events)
checklist.where: Three items only, each to a T1 SEC filing: EUR2.55bn bond admission to trading, 1 Sep 2026 [^19], used in "## Investment Thesis" pillar "Funding is debt-led and working capital is tight"; Etcamah US approval in HR+ breast cancer, 8 Sep 2026 [^17]; Imfinzi+Imdelltra overall-survival result in small cell lung cancer, 8 Sep 2026 [^111]. All three appear in the "## Sources" table with artefact hashes. Materially incomplete for the window: no H1 2026 results (AZN reports its half year inside the 11 Jun–11 Sep window), no deals, no litigation or investigation development, and "## Catalysts" is stamped "Insufficient evidence".

checklist.item: management or board changes in the last year
checklist.where: "## Management & Governance" → Commentary: "Evidence available for this note does not include specific information on AstraZeneca's board composition, named executive officers, their tenure or track record, or the design of executive incentive arrangements", and "No compensation figures, equity award data, or say-on-pay outcomes were available to cite." The Governance Observations bullets only restate that the detail sits in the incorporated-by-reference Annual Report. No director, no officer, no appointment or departure is named.

checklist.item: capital allocation: buybacks, dividends, capex, acquisitions, with figures
checklist.where: "## Capital Allocation" → Commentary and Figures table (lines listing "Dividends paid, FY2025 | $4,971m", "Proceeds from debt, FY2025 | $15m", etc.) — the entire section, commentary and table alike, carries not a single footnote marker, uniquely in this document. Dividends and debt movements are separately sourced in "## Cash Flow Analysis" ([^83]–[^89]), so the figures are traceable elsewhere; but the dividend rates "1.03 dollars per share and 2.10 dollars per share" and the claim "no share repurchases have been made since 2012" are cited nowhere. Capex and acquisitions have no figures at all: "The evidence available does not include a breakdown of investing cash flow between capital expenditure, acquisitions, and portfolio transactions."

checklist.item: the key risks the company itself names in its latest annual filing
checklist.where: "## Key Risks" → Risks table, row "Adverse outcome of litigation or governmental investigations", attributed to "its Form 20-F dated February 24, 2026" and footnoted [^103] to the 20-F URL. Thin and partly uncited elsewhere: "## Growth Outlook" → "**What constrains durability:**" paraphrases the manufacturing/supply-interruption and IT-attack risk factors with no footnote marker at all, and "## Earnings Quality" attributes the Fusion multi-period excess earnings method assumptions and legal-provisioning judgement to "The 20-F" in prose with no marker. Only two or three of the filing's named principal risks are reproduced; there is no risk-factor inventory, and four of the six Key Risks rows are analyst-constructed from ratios rather than company-named.

checklist.item: competitive position with named competitors
checklist.where: "## Industry & Competitive Positioning" → "### Competitive Position": not one competitor is named anywhere in the section or the document. It says only that AZN "competes across oncology, biopharmaceuticals, and rare disease with a portfolio built substantially on biologics and specialty small molecules" and then pivots into FY2025 margins and leverage ratios — the company's own financials, not a competitive comparison. "## Comparable companies" confirms the gap: "every one of the eight proposed peers was excluded", and the peers are not even listed by name.

checklist.item: regulatory or legal matters currently open
checklist.where: "## Key Risks" → Risks table row on litigation, sourced to the 20-F [^103], establishes only the generic standing exposure ("subject to extensive regulation, litigation and governmental investigation"). No specific open matter is identified — no case, docket, agency inquiry, or contingent-liability item; the same section states the material "does not itemise product-level exclusivity dates, biosimilar filing dockets, China-specific investigations or tariff schedules". "## Industry & Competitive Positioning" likewise: "does not identify which, if any, AstraZeneca products appear by name on a published CMS selected-drug list". The two product-regulatory items cited (8 Sep 2026) are, on the note's own account in "## Catalysts", "past events rather than forward catalysts".

checklist.item: a valuation with stated assumptions and a per-share result
checklist.where: "## Valuation — Discounted Cash Flow": "No discounted cash flow was produced, so there are no valuation figures to interpret", and "### How These Figures Were Produced": "The valuation needs a share count for the year ending 31 December 2025 and the filings carry none — neither diluted, basic nor a plain outstanding figure." That stated reason does not survive the document's own figures: net income $10,225m over diluted EPS of $6.54 implies roughly 1,563m diluted shares, and dividends paid $4,971m over DPS of $1.03 + $2.10 implies about the same — so a share count is derivable from facts already on the page. No multiple, no price, no yield, no target, despite a T4 licensed daily price series to 2026-09-11 sitting in the "## Sources" table ([^114]) unused. "## Comparable companies": "No comparable figure was computed."

checklist.item: a bear case with a number attached
checklist.where: "## Scenarios & Sensitivities" → "**Bear case:**" and "## Investment Thesis" → pillar "Bear proposition: US pricing mechanics compress the margin path". A bear case exists in the body and is argued mechanically (committed R&D of 14.2bn and SG&A of 19.9bn mean "lost revenue drops through with little cushion"). But every number attached is an FY2025 actual used as an anchor — the Scenarios table labels them "(structural anchor)" and "(downside cushion)" — not a bear-case output: no revenue decline, no margin level, no EPS, no per-share downside. The note concedes the drivers are unsourced: "every driver assumption in them is analyst-set rather than filed", and "### Sensitivity Commentary" adds "no per-point sensitivity is quantified". So the bear case has actuals attached, not a bear number.

verifiability.how_a_figure_is_checked: Almost every figure in the tables carries a footnote of one of two shapes. (a) A stored fact: a T1 SEC URL — either the XBRL company-facts JSON for CIK 0000901832 or the 20-F at sec.gov/Archives/.../azn-20251231x20f.htm — with publish and retrieval dates, tier, and an artefact hash in the "## Sources" table (e.g. `f8ee3de56da6` for the company facts). (b) A recorded calculation: formula, value, period and code version, e.g. [^80] "`current ratio = current assets / current liabilities` = 0.9381 ... (`aer.calc.ratios:current_ratio`, code version `6d9c6c80d78a`)". So the audit path is real and unusually explicit. Two frictions matter. Fact footnotes name neither the XBRL tag nor the value, so you must search a very large JSON for the number yourself; 20-F citations give a document URL with no page, section or excerpt. And calculation footnotes do not cite their own inputs, so a ratio is only checkable by re-deriving it from figures elsewhere in the note. Three things are not checkable at all: the entire "## Capital Allocation" section has no footnotes (including the $1.03 and $2.10 dividend rates and "no share repurchases... since 2012"), "basic earnings of $6.60 per share" in "## Growth Outlook" is unsourced and sits oddly beside the DCF section's claim that no basic figure exists in the filings, and the two chart blocks ("### Segment mix", "### Revenue and margin history") carry 39 footnotes between them but no visible data — "*Rendered in the HTML and PDF editions of this report.*"
verifiability.figures_checked: I recomputed the FY2025 set from the note's own inputs and it is internally coherent: gross margin 48,106/58,739 = 81.90%; operating 13,743/58,739 = 23.40%; net 10,225/58,739 = 17.41%; EBITDA margin 18,829/58,739 = 32.06%; interest cover 13,743/1,694 = 8.11x; net debt/EBITDA 23,911/18,829 = 1.270x; current ratio 28,723/30,617 = 0.938x; quick ratio (5,711+30+15,177)/30,617 = 0.683x; ROIC 11,339/72,578 = 15.62%; equity from 114,074 − 65,355 = 48,719, giving ROE 21.0% and ROA 9.0%; debt/equity 0.6087 implies total debt ~29.6bn, which less cash of 5,711 reproduces net debt of 23,911. Dividends of $3.13/share on ~1,563m implied shares reproduces $4,971m paid. Two checks failed. (1) "## Capital Allocation" says investing and financing "together exceeding operating cash generation for the year" — 6,808 + 7,544 = 14,352, which is below operating cash flow of 14,575, so the sentence and the inference it supports ("both consistent with the net cash outflow implied by...") are wrong. (2) The nine red-team "contradictions" in "## Validation & Disagreements" appear to be period mismatches, not errors: their own footnotes resolve to earlier years — [^107] net debt/EBITDA 3.2233 is FY2021, [^108] current ratio 1.1615 is FY2021, [^109] ROIC 0.0823 is FY2022, [^110] gross margin 0.6676 is FY2021, [^113] cash conversion 53.2411 is FY2021 — and footnotes [^55]–[^69] show the gross-margin series rising 0.6676 (FY2021) → 0.8195 (FY2023) → 0.819 (FY2025), which is exactly the FY2025 figure the red team says is unsupported. I could not verify any figure against the SEC source itself under the read-only constraint.
