Adjudication of the nine escalated disagreements, including the GSPC.INDX close conflict (7656.98 vs 7672.54) — all nine are still "Escalated for human decision at approval"
rubric.first_thing_to_check: Open the cited XBRL company-facts JSON for CIK 0000901832 and confirm FY2025 revenue of $58,739m, gross profit of $48,106m and operating income of $13,743m, then read the red-team footnotes ([^107]–[^110], [^113]) to confirm that their "recorded" contradictions are FY2021/FY2022 calculations being compared against FY2025 claims. Everything in the note hangs on this: if the red team is right, "the profitability core of the thesis is unevidenced" on its own account; if it is a period mismatch, the note shipped nine unresolved severity-3-to-5 objections that were never adjudicated, which is a different kind of defect but still one that must be closed before any figure here is quoted onward.
rubric.strongest_paragraph: "## Earnings Quality" → the second paragraph, "Those intangibles rest on unobservable inputs." It is the one place the note does analysis rather than description: it names the valuation technique the filing used for the Fusion development-stage intangibles (multi-period excess earnings), names the three assumptions it turns on (probability of technical and regulatory success, peak-year sales, revenue erosion), and then attaches a specific dated fact — "One acquired programme was terminated and written off in full in December 2024, only months after the business was consolidated from June 2024" — and draws the correct, falsifiable inference: "a fast reversal of purchase-price allocation judgement, and a caution on the carrying value of what remains." That connects a governance-of-estimates point to a real impairment risk on $37,846m of intangibles and $21,242m of goodwill. Runner-up is the leverage-definition paragraph in "## Balance Sheet & Liquidity", which states its own net debt basis, says AZN's own measure "lands modestly below the figure used here", and refuses to treat the balance sheet as settled. Both deserve a caveat: neither paragraph carries a footnote marker, so their 20-F attributions are prose, not verified citations.
rubric.weakest_paragraph: "## Capital Allocation" → Commentary. It is the only section in the document with no citation of any kind, and it is also the one that gets its arithmetic wrong: "Investing activities consumed 6,808 million dollars, while financing activities absorbed 7,544 million dollars, together exceeding operating cash generation for the year" — 14,352 against 14,575, so they did not, and the later inference that the cash and short-term-investment declines are "both consistent with the net cash outflow implied by investing and financing activity exceeding operating cash flow" rests on that error (the note's own "## Cash Flow Analysis" reaches the opposite reading, "the structural signature of a self-funding cash cycle"). It then closes on "a substantial and growing distribution" — a growth claim in a document that elsewhere insists "no prior-year comparatives" exist and "no growth rate is asserted and none should be inferred" — and its two most checkable specifics, the $1.03 and $2.10 per-share dividend rates and "no share repurchases have been made since 2012", are attributed only to "a disclosure in the annual report" with no footnote. Confident prose, no evidence trail, and a sign error in the one calculation it attempts.
rubric.overall:
Judged as a research note against this brief, the document is a well-instrumented audit trail wrapped around very little research. The machinery is genuinely good: nearly every figure carries either a T1 SEC URL with an artefact hash or a formula footnote with inputs' period and code version; the FY2025 ratio set is arithmetically coherent when re-derived; definitional choices are disclosed rather than buried (NOPAT construction, closing rather than average capital, net debt scope, the admission that stricter lease- and pension-inclusive conventions "would show leverage appreciably higher"); and the note refuses several tempting fabrications outright — no apportioned regional revenue, no invented catalyst calendar, no DCF, no per-point sensitivity. That discipline is rare and should be credited.

But the brief asked three questions and the note answers one and a half. Patent-expiry exposure — the first question — is not answered at all: no medicine named, no expiry date, no exposed revenue, only a well-written statement that the evidence "does not extend to product-level or geographic revenue detail". The oncology question is answered only at the meta level: the note correctly reports that pipeline contribution is assumption rather than record, and then quantifies neither the assumption nor the record. The balance-sheet question is answered for FY2025 and not for the horizon, because there is no capex line, no free cash flow, no forward commitment, and the September 2026 EUR2.55bn bond is cited but never carried into a single leverage figure. Six of the ten checklist items are absent, one is unsourced, and the three that are present-sourced are thin.

Crucially, the evidence base is not merely sparse — it is narrow by choice. Six sources, of which one 20-F and one XBRL JSON do nearly all the work. The 20-F's revenue note, therapy-area review and governance report are repeatedly described as "incorporated by reference" and then never fetched, which is where the segment split, the IP schedule and the board detail all live. A licensed daily price series to the as-of date sits in the Sources table and is used for nothing, while the valuation section declines to produce a per-share figure on the stated ground that no share count exists in the filings — a claim refuted twice over by the note's own numbers (net income over diluted EPS, and dividends paid over dividend per share, both imply about 1,563m shares). No H1 2026 interim is present, so an 11 September 2026 note runs on figures to 31 December 2025 and Q2 2025.

The document also contradicts itself on load-bearing points. "Growth is unevidenced... no prior-period comparatives" and "the annual record in hand covers that single year. There is no comparable prior-year column" sit on the same pages as a five-year revenue history table and a five-year margin series in footnotes [^55]–[^69]. "No invested-capital, cost-of-capital or return-on-invested-capital figure is on record" sits two sections away from "a return on invested capital of 15.6%" built on "invested capital of $72,578m". The header declares "no view reached" while the Investment Thesis says "Our central view is that..." and threatens to "lower our fair value" — a fair value that exists nowhere. And the note ships with nine unresolved red-team objections, four at severity 4 or 5, one of which states flatly that "the profitability core of the thesis is unevidenced" — all "Escalated for human decision at approval". On inspection those objections look like period-mismatch artefacts (their own footnotes resolve to FY2021 and FY2022 calculations), which is a point in the prose's favour and against the validator; but either way a reader is handed a document whose internal QA says its headline margins may be wrong, with no adjudication.

Net: honest about its gaps to a degree most notes are not, and traceable where it does commit to a number — but as an answer to this brief it is a scaffold. There is no view, no valuation, no price, no competitor, no product, no expiry date, and a bear case whose only numbers are last year's actuals.

rubric.first_thing_to_check: The share basis behind the per-share outputs, against an actual quote. The header calls the security "AZN (NYSE)" — the ADR — but §Valuation divides equity value by "Shares outstanding 1,562,000,000", the ordinary count, and no share price, market capitalisation or implied upside appears anywhere in 769 lines. One NYSE ADR is half an ordinary share, so $169.80 is either roughly fair value against the London line (~£130 ≈ $175) or 100% upside against the ~$85 ADR. Nothing else in the note is decision-relevant until that is settled.
rubric.strongest_paragraph: §Valuation — Discounted Cash Flow, "Recorded Caveats" (the four bullets). It states that book equity was used as the equity weight so "the equity weight is understated, the debt weight overstated, and the resulting WACC too low. Every valuation discounted at it is correspondingly too high"; that "more than three quarters of the enterprise value is terminal value... the answer rests almost entirely on the terminal assumption"; that the two methods "disagree by more than a quarter... the distance between them is the honest width of the answer"; and that the enterprise-to-equity bridge is net debt alone, so associates, minorities and pension deficits are ignored. Four sentences that tell the reader precisely why not to trust the number the same section publishes. Runner-up is §Growth Outlook's "the pipeline is carried at zero contribution rather than at an assumed one" — a direct answer to focus question 2, undermined only by the DCF's 11.9% growth.
rubric.weakest_paragraph: §Validation & Disagreements, the eight "Red team" entries (lines beginning "Red team — balance sheet, severity 5/5" through "Red team — valuation, severity 4/5"). They assert that essentially every headline figure in the note is wrong — gross margin 0.668/0.721 not 81.9%, operating margin 0.028/0.085 not 23.4%, interest cover 0.812 not 8.11x, net debt/EBITDA 3.223 not 1.27x, ROIC 0.0823 not 15.6%, free cash flow $4,872m not $11,765m — and conclude "earnings do not cover interest and leverage is not modest". Every one is marked "Escalated for human decision at approval" and none is resolved. Yet their own footnotes give the game away: [^143] is FY2021 interest cover, [^145] is FY2021 gross margin, [^146] is FY2021 free cash flow, [^148] is FY2022 ROIC — the red team compared FY2025 claims against FY2021/FY2022 calculations, and the note's own footnote history ([^39]–[^53]) shows FY2025 values are recorded. So the document publishes six severity-3-to-5 accusations that its own evidence contradicts, leaves them unresolved, and thereby destroys the reader's ability to rely on any number in it. A close second for sheer uselessness is §Business Overview's single 600-word paragraph, which spends its length on what cannot be established and includes process advice to a future researcher ("Any register search intended to trace applicant-of-record status... should therefore not be limited to the parent company name alone").
rubric.overall:
Unusually honest, and largely unusable. The document's real achievement is epistemic hygiene: every figure carries a footnote to either an SEC artefact with a URL and hash or a named calculation module with formula and code version; the arithmetic reconciles when you check it (48,106/58,739 = 81.9%, 14,575 − 2,810 = 11,765, 13,743/1,694 = 8.11, 0.048 + 0.4×0.045 = 0.066, and the FY2021–24 revenue series matches AstraZeneca's actual reported revenue); it refuses to invent what it lacks, saying "unresolved" where a sell-side note would assert; and its Recorded Caveats tell you its own valuation is biased high. Three of fourteen sections carry explicit degradation banners, and it says so at the top.

But the brief asked three questions and the note answers one and a half. Focus question 1 — patent-expiry exposure inside the horizon, the reason anyone underwrites AstraZeneca in 2026 — gets four separate declarations that it cannot be answered. No product is named with a revenue figure; Tagrisso, Farxiga and Imfinzi appear once, in a sentence saying their revenue is unavailable; no expiry date appears anywhere. The stated reason is that the 20-F carries the Therapy Area Review and revenue note by incorporation by reference — but AstraZeneca's FY2025 results announcement lists product revenue line by line, so this is a retrieval limit presented as a disclosure limit. Focus question 3 is answered with real, footnoted figures (FCF $11,765m against dividends $4,971m, with R&D already inside operating cash flow) and then contradicted three times in the same document: §Balance Sheet says "Interest cover is not established by the figures available, and no view is offered on it here" while two other sections publish 8.11x; §Growth Outlook says to treat balance-sheet capacity as "an open question, not a settled strength"; and the severity-5 red-team item says earnings do not cover interest at all.

The internal contradictions are not confined to that. Beta is 0.4 in the cost-of-capital table and 0.3 in the Prior Research Comparison; capex intensity is 0.033377 in one and 0.05 in the other. §Growth Outlook says the pipeline is "carried at zero contribution" while the DCF holds 11.9% revenue growth flat for five years — which is precisely an assumption about pipeline replacement, and which I had to reverse-engineer as the FY2021–25 revenue CAGR (11.94%) because the "stated justification" is referenced but never printed. The 14.2% forecast EBIT margin is likewise the five-year average operating margin, including the Alexion-distorted 2021, and sits nine points below the FY2025 actual with no comment. Mechanically extrapolating a historical CAGR is the one thing a patent-cliff question forbids, and the note does it without saying so.

Then the omissions a private investor cannot work around: no share price, no market cap, no implied upside on a $169.80/$333.48 pair that differ by a factor of two; the ordinary-versus-ADR share-basis trap; no management guidance of any kind; no named competitor in a section titled "Industry & Competitive Positioning"; no executive or director named, not even the CEO; all eight proposed peers excluded and not listed; no dated catalyst inside the twelve-month horizon, which is the horizon; and a financial base that stops at December 2025, nine months before the as-of date, with H1 2026 results absent and the note flagging that its picture "may be stale". Three exhibits are replaced by "*Rendered in the HTML and PDF editions*", one of them substituting a 100-word data-licence notice for the football field.

Against a Claude subscription as the alternative: a single well-framed session would have produced the product-level revenue split, the LOE schedule, the H1 2026 print and FY2026 guidance, the $80bn 2030 ambition, named competitors and a price comparison — the whole of focus question 1 and the missing half of question 3 — in an hour, without the sourcing discipline. What this note has that a chat session does not is verifiable provenance and a refusal to bluff. What it lacks is the content. I would keep its Recorded Caveats as a template for how to disclose a DCF's weaknesses, take its FY2025 income-statement and cash-flow base as a checkable starting point, and do the exposure work myself.

verifiability.how_a_figure_is_checked: Two routes, and the note is built for both. (1) Recalculation: every derived figure carries a footnote with the formula, the value, the period, the producing module and a code version — e.g. [^5] "gross margin = gross profit / revenue = 0.819 ... for FY2025 (aer.calc.ratios:gross_margin, code version 4c63dbfc4794)" — and §Historical Financial Analysis "Financial History" prints the inputs, so 48,106/58,739 = 0.8190, 13,743/58,739 = 0.2340, 14,575 − 2,810 = 11,765, 13,743/1,694 = 8.113, 23,911/18,829 = 1.270, 28,723/30,617 = 0.9381, and 0.0663×0.6216 + 0.04524×0.3784 = 0.0583 can all be verified with a calculator in seconds. Every one I checked reconciles. (2) Tracing to primary source: facts point to "ASTRAZENECA PLC XBRL company facts, US Securities and Exchange Commission, published 24 February 2026" at https://data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/companyfacts/CIK0000901832.json, narrative to the 20-F at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/901832/000110465926019130/azn-20251231x20f.htm, and the §Sources table adds artefact hashes (f8ee3de56da6, 5f65a1e4d20e). This route is slower than it should be: the companyfacts endpoint is one very large JSON covering every tag and period with no tag name, unit or fact identifier given in the footnote, and the 20-F citations give no item number, page or quoted excerpt, so a risk-language claim means reading the filing. Route (1) also only proves internal consistency — it cannot catch a mis-mapped XBRL tag, which is precisely what the eight unresolved red-team entries allege.
verifiability.figures_checked: I re-derived roughly a dozen figures from the note's own printed inputs and all reconciled: gross margin 81.9% (48,106/58,739), operating margin 23.4% (13,743/58,739), net margin 17.4% (10,225/58,739), EBITDA margin 32.1% (18,829/58,739), free cash flow $11,765m (14,575 − 2,810), net debt/EBITDA 1.27x, interest cover 8.11x (13,743/1,694), current ratio 0.9381 (28,723/30,617), cost of equity 6.63% (4.8% + 0.4×4.5%) and WACC 5.83%. I also sanity-checked the FY2021–FY2024 revenue series ($37,417m / $44,351m / $45,811m / $54,073m) and the depressed FY2021 margins against AstraZeneca's actual reported results — they match, so the underlying facts look genuine and the red team's contradictory values are the real FY2021/FY2022 figures compared against FY2025 claims. What does not reconcile is between sections: beta 0.4 in §Valuation versus "Confirmed at 0.3" in §Prior Research Comparison; capex intensity 0.033377 versus "Confirmed at 0.05"; "Interest cover is not established by the figures available" in §Balance Sheet versus 8.11x in §Earnings Quality and §Growth Outlook; "the pipeline is carried at zero contribution" in §Growth Outlook versus 11.9% revenue growth held flat for five years in §Valuation; and share repurchases of $0 in §Capital Allocation versus $489m and $81m in the run's own index. I could not check any per-share output at all: no share price, market capitalisation or share-class basis is given, which the valuation red-team entry also flags — "no per-share output can be checked at all".

verifiability.how_a_figure_is_checked: Every figure carries a superscript into a 148-entry "## Notes" list, and the notes come in two shapes. A fact note gives title, publisher, publication date, retrieval date, evidence tier and a live URL (e.g. [^24] "ASTRAZENECA PLC XBRL company facts, US Securities and Exchange Commission, published 24 February 2026, retrieved 11 September 2026, tier T1_REGULATORY" with the data.sec.gov companyfacts link), and "## Sources" adds an artefact hash per document. A calculated note gives the formula, the value, the period, the module and a code version (e.g. [^57] "interest cover = operating income / interest expense = 8.1128 ... for FY2025"). That second shape is genuinely useful: because the inputs are printed in the same tables, most ratios can be recomputed on paper without leaving the document. Source-level facts are much weaker — all of them point at one multi-megabyte XBRL JSON endpoint with no XBRL tag, element name, context or section pointer, so "revenue was 58,739" is not practically checkable from the citation given, and the 20-F citations point at the whole filing rather than a page or item. Two footnote defects: [^102] is labelled "the filed count: diluted_shares_outstanding" but resolves to a value-per-share calculation of 333.476; and the red-team footnotes [^143]–[^148] each resolve to a single prior-year calculation (FY2021 interest cover, FY2021 gross margin, FY2021 free cash flow, FY2022 ROIC) that does not cover most of the figures the disagreement text quotes.

rubric.first_thing_to_check: The severity 5/5 entry in \"## Validation & Disagreements\": whether the \"recorded interest_cover calculation is 0.812\" and \"net_debt_to_ebitda is 3.223\" are FY2025 figures or prior-year ones. Footnote [^143] attached to that very entry resolves to \"interest cover = operating income / interest expense = 0.8123 ... for FY2021\", which points to a period mismatch rather than a restatement — yet the document presents it as an unresolved reversal of its own solvency conclusion and leaves it \"Escalated for human decision at approval\". Until that is settled, the answer to the brief's third question is not merely uncertain, it is given twice in opposite directions, and the same doubt attaches to the margins, ROIC and free cash flow that the rest of the note is built on.
rubric.strongest_paragraph: \"## Valuation — Discounted Cash Flow\", the Commentary paragraph beginning \"The most important thing this framework cannot do is separate the portfolio into its parts.\" It explains why a single blended growth rate cannot represent exclusivity decline and pipeline replacement at the same time, warns the reader not to treat the per-share outputs as a sum of those parts, notes that the company's own impairment models work asset by asset with \"probability of technical and regulatory success and sales erosion curves following patent expiry\", and then identifies a bias specific to this industry: \"R&D of $14.2 billion on revenue of $58.7 billion is expensed inside the EBIT margin, so the model pays in full for the pipeline each year while crediting it only through the growth rate. Where growth is set conservatively, that biases the value downward.\" It reasons about the company's economics rather than about data availability, and it is the one place the note tells you which way its own method is wrong. The four \"### Recorded Caveats\" just above it are nearly as good — particularly the admission that book-value equity weighting makes the WACC \"too low\" so \"every valuation discounted at it is correspondingly too high\".
rubric.weakest_paragraph: \"## Earnings Quality\" Commentary, at the sentence \"Interest cover of 8.11x relates EBITDA of $18,829m to interest expense of $1,694m.\" That ratio is 11.1, not 8.11; the figure's own footnote defines it as operating income over interest expense; and the paragraph then builds a caution on the mislabelling — that a reader preferring \"a cover ratio struck on operating income of $13,743m\" would reach \"a materially lower figure\" — which is precisely inverted, since $13,743m is already the numerator. The Red Flags bullet repeats the error as fact (\"Coverage and leverage ratios cited here are EBITDA-based\"). A close second is the \"## Business Overview\" Commentary: one unbroken block of roughly 700 words that never names a product, a therapy area or a geography, and instead advises that \"Any register search intended to trace applicant-of-record status for AstraZeneca products should therefore not be limited to the parent company name alone\" — research process notes standing where a description of the business belongs.
rubric.overall: This reads as a scrupulous note about the absence of evidence rather than a research note on AstraZeneca. Its discipline is real and unusual: near-total footnote coverage, formula-and-inputs notes that let a reader recompute most ratios on paper, explicit refusals to compute a growth rate from two observations or to tabulate expiries it cannot source, and caveats that name the direction of their own bias (book-value WACC \"too low\", so \"every valuation discounted at it is correspondingly too high\"). Where it commits to figures they mostly hold up — I rebuilt invested capital, ROIC, EPS, WACC and five ratios from numbers printed in the document. But the brief is largely unmet. Question one comes back blank by the note's own admission, four times over. Question two is answered only in the sense that the note declines to size the pipeline at all and rests every forecast dollar on one operator-confirmed 11.9% growth rate whose justification is not printed. Question three is answered three incompatible ways and left \"escalated for human decision\" with no decision recorded. Six of the ten checklist items are absent or effectively so, including segment revenue, guidance, named competitors, and any board or management detail. Trust then takes two further hits. First, the note carries eight unresolved internal contradictions — a severity 5/5 entry asserting that \"earnings do not cover interest and leverage is not modest\", another that \"No recorded calculation reproduces any draft figure\" for every headline margin — while the footnotes behind them resolve to FY2021 and FY2022 calculations, strongly suggesting period mismatch. Handing a reader that alarm without resolving it is worse than either answer would have been. Second, verifiable errors survive: the interest-cover mislabelling and the inverted argument built on it, a net debt figure $1.8bn away from its own printed components, beta and capex intensity stated two different ways, and a footnote labelled \"shares outstanding\" that resolves to a value-per-share calculation. Practically, 148 footnotes rest on four distinct documents — one XBRL endpoint, a 20-F read only for risk language, two press releases dated 8 September 2026, and a price series that is never shown — and three exhibits are missing from this edition. With no share price anywhere, the $169.80–$333.48 range cannot be positioned against anything, which for a 12-month-horizon note is disqualifying on its own. The header's \"Non-binding view: no view reached\" is, in the end, the most accurate line in it — and it sits oddly against the Investment Thesis, which does state a view (\"a constructive but low-confidence view: the returns are proven, the durability is not\") and argues it properly, with four named falsifiers under \"What Would Change The View\".

focus_questions.question: Is the oncology pipeline's contribution to growth sourced from approvals and launches, or from assumptions about them?
focus_questions.where: "Growth Outlook" → "Oncology, as disclosed" and "Base case"; "Valuation — Discounted Cash Flow" → Commentary, paragraph beginning "The most important thing this framework cannot do is separate the portfolio into its parts"; Investment Thesis pillar 3.
focus_questions.with_what_evidence: Two dated primary events, both sourced to SEC-archived releases of 8 September 2026 with URLs: the Etcamah US approval in HR+ breast cancer [^20] and Imfinzi + Imdelltra overall-survival data in small-cell lung cancer [^142]. Neither carries revenue, peak-sales or launch economics, and the note says so: "no roster of pivotal-stage assets, no list of filed applications, no published regulatory action dates, and no company-stated revenue ambition attached to a named asset". It then declares "the pipeline is carried at zero contribution rather than at an assumed one" — which cannot be literally true alongside a confirmed five-year revenue growth assumption of 11.9% held flat, on a base the note elsewhere says it cannot decompose. The valuation commentary concedes exactly this: "A single revenue growth path cannot simultaneously represent decline in marketed products as exclusivity lapses and replacement of that revenue by pipeline assets" and "pipeline contribution is implicit rather than isolated". So the question is answered, but by admission: the contribution is assumption, not sourced launch economics. Neither component is sized, and the 11.9% growth rate's justification is not printed (only "proposed by aer.services.assumption_proposals with a stated justification").

verifiability.how_a_figure_is_checked: Three routes, none of which gets you to a line in a document. (1) Reported line items — revenue, cost of revenue, R&D, SG&A, operating income, net income, EPS, cash, current assets and liabilities, debt, dividends, capex — all cite one of two identical entries for https://data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/companyfacts/CIK0000901832.json (artefact `f8ee3de56da6`), with no XBRL concept name, no context or period id and no unit. You must download a multi-megabyte JSON of every tagged fact across all years and hunt for a matching value, with no way to confirm which tag was used — which matters, because the same note reports gross margin of 66.8% for FY2021 and 82.0% for FY2023, a 15-point jump that either reflects genuine Alexion-era amortisation in cost of sales or unstable tag mapping, and nothing printed lets you tell. (2) Derived figures cite a formula, a module and a code version (e.g. "`interest cover = operating income / interest expense` = 8.1128 ... `aer.calc.ratios:interest_cover`, code version `4c63dbfc4794`") but never the input fact ids, so you can only check the arithmetic against other printed figures, not against the source. (3) Narrative claims cite the whole 20-F .htm URL with no item, page or quoted excerpt — a text search of a large filing. The per-share outputs are the worst case: [^100] gives only `aer.calc.dcf:value_per_share`, and enterprise value, equity value, the five forecast years' free cash flows and the denominators behind "depreciation intensity 0.114739" and "capex intensity 0.033377" appear nowhere, so $169.80 cannot be reproduced from anything in the document at any price in time.
verifiability.figures_checked: I checked internal arithmetic where the document supplies both sides. Consistent: 48,106/58,739 = 81.90% gross margin; 13,743/58,739 = 23.40%; 10,225/58,739 = 17.41%; 18,829/58,739 = 32.06% (printed 32.1%); 13,743/1,694 = 8.11x; 23,911/18,829 = 1.27x; 28,723/30,617 = 0.9381 (printed 0.94); 10,225/6.54 = 1,563m shares against the 1,562m used in the DCF; Ke = 0.0483 + 0.4 x 0.045 = 0.0663. Inconsistent: the Earnings Quality prose says "Interest cover of 8.11x relates EBITDA of $18,829m to interest expense of $1,694m" — that quotient is 11.1x, and footnote [^57] shows the ratio is struck on operating income, so the note mislabels its own coverage measure and repeats the error in Red Flags. NOPAT of $11.34bn against operating income of $13,743m implies a 17.5% tax rate, not the 20% stated in the assumptions table, though it is internally consistent with ROIC 15.6% on invested capital of $72,578m. Pre-tax income $12,402m less tax $2,169m = $10,233m against net income of $10,225m (minorities, presumably, unstated). Not checkable at all: $169.80 and $333.48 per share, the 25 heatmap cells, and every FY2021–FY2024 figure in the revenue history, since no per-period source reference is given.

They cite FY2021 and FY2022 calculations (interest cover 0.8123, gross margin 0.6676, free cash flow $4,872m, ROIC 0.0823) and those values match the FY2021/FY2022 columns of the note's own margin history [^39]–[^53] exactly. So the run appears to have compared FY2021/FY2022 recorded calculations against FY2025 claims and concluded the FY2025 claims are false. Nothing else in the note is worth reading until that is settled, because as shipped the document asserts both that its gross margin is 81.9% and that \"no recorded calculation reproduces any draft figure\" and that the profitability picture \"may be materially overstated\" — unresolved, \"Escalated for human decision at approval\" — while the metrics table simultaneously reports citation_accuracy 1.00, cited_figure_agreement 0 and numerical_consistency 0, all passing.
rubric.strongest_paragraph: \"Valuation — Discounted Cash Flow\" → Commentary, the paragraph beginning \"The most important thing this framework cannot do is separate the portfolio into its parts.\" It names precisely why the model cannot answer the brief's first two questions — \"A single revenue growth path cannot simultaneously represent decline in marketed products as exclusivity lapses and replacement of that revenue by pipeline assets; the two are netted into one rate\" — tells the reader not to read the output as a sum of parts, contrasts the approach with the company's own asset-by-asset impairment modelling using \"probability of technical and regulatory success and sales erosion curves following patent expiry\", and then identifies the direction of the resulting bias: R&D is expensed inside the EBIT margin, so \"the model pays in full for the pipeline each year while crediting it only through the growth rate\". That is a genuine argument about its own method, with a sign attached, and it is reinforced by the \"Recorded Caveats\" immediately above, which quantify the weakness of the output (\"More than three quarters of the enterprise value is terminal value\", \"The two terminal methods disagree by more than a quarter\", book-value weighting makes every discounted value \"too high\").
rubric.weakest_paragraph: \"Earnings Quality\" → Commentary: a single ~600-word block that contains the note's one outright arithmetic falsehood. \"Interest cover of 8.11x relates EBITDA of $18,829m to interest expense of $1,694m\" — that division gives 11.1x, and footnote [^57] states the formula is operating income / interest expense. The paragraph then builds on the mislabel, warning that \"a reader who prefers a cover ratio struck on operating income of $13,743m... will reach a materially lower figure\", when operating income is exactly what produced the 8.11x quoted; the Red Flags bullet repeats it (\"Coverage and leverage ratios cited here are EBITDA-based\"). Since coverage is load-bearing for focus question 3, a misdescribed coverage ratio is not a cosmetic slip. Runner-up for weakest: \"Business Overview\" → Commentary, a 600-word unbroken paragraph on a company whose therapy areas, products and geographies are never named, which instead advises that \"any register search intended to trace applicant-of-record status for AstraZeneca products should therefore not be limited to the parent company name alone\" — housekeeping for a different task, occupying the section that should carry the business.
rubric.overall:
Unusually honest about what it does not know, and unusable as a result — and the honesty is itself unreliable, because the note contradicts itself on what it knows.

What it has: one primary financial source (the SEC XBRL companyfacts JSON), the 20-F of 24 February 2026 for risk language, two SEC-archived press releases of 8 September 2026, and a price series that appears in no figure. Six source rows, four of them the same issuer. Off that base it produces an internally consistent FY2025 income statement, cash flow and balance sheet read, a five-year revenue and margin history, a fully specified DCF with provenance on every assumption, and a candid caveat block. The discipline on derived figures — formula, module, code version — is better than most sell-side work, and the refusals are the right refusals: it declines to tabulate expiry dates it does not have and declines to size the pipeline it cannot source, where a worse note would have invented both.

What sinks it. First, the note disagrees with itself on its own central facts. The Executive Summary says "No discount rate, terminal growth assumption, invested capital, return on invested capital, share price or share count is available" and that "no per-share output... is defensible here", while the At-a-glance table prints WACC 5.8% and "Value per share (base) $169.80", the thesis cites invested capital of $72.6bn and ROIC 15.6%, and the valuation section prints terminal growth 2.5%, 1,562m shares and two per-share values. The header says "Non-binding view: no view reached"; the Investment Thesis says "we hold a constructive but low-confidence view". Historical Financial Analysis says the history "covers the year ended 31 December 2025 only" while At a glance shows FY2021–FY2025 revenue. Balance Sheet & Liquidity says "Interest cover is not established by the figures available"; three other sections quote 8.11x. These are not caveats, they are contradictions, and a reader cannot tell which half to believe.

Second, the run publishes eight unresolved red-team disagreements that assert the headline numbers are wrong — "Every headline profitability figure in the draft is contradicted by the run's own recorded calculations", "On the recorded numbers, earnings do not cover interest and leverage is not modest" — all "Escalated for human decision at approval" and none decided. On inspection the supporting footnotes are FY2021/FY2022 calculations being compared with FY2025 claims, so the escalations look spurious; but the document ships them next to a metrics table reporting perfect citation accuracy and zero figure disagreement, and does not reconcile the two. Either the numbers are wrong or the validator is, and the note takes no position.

Third, against the brief specifically: no product or segment revenue, no expiry date, no guidance, no H1 2026 results, no named competitor, no named legal matter, no dated catalyst (that section cites zero sources), no bear-case number, and no share price — so two per-share figures 96% apart, both of which the note says are biased high, cannot be converted into any decision. Focus question 1 is unanswered, 2 is answered by conceding the growth rate does the work, 3 is answered for a year that closed nine months before the as-of date. The as-of date is also 12 September 2026 rather than the brief's 11 September, and "Point-in-time: enforced" sits beside look_ahead_recall "not exercised".

As a process artefact it is interesting and mostly trustworthy about its own limits. As a research note for this brief it establishes that AstraZeneca was a high-margin, cash-generative business in FY2025 and that nothing else in the brief could be answered from what was gathered. That is a finding about the evidence base, not about the company.

focus_questions.question: How exposed is revenue to the patent expiries falling due inside the horizon?
focus_questions.where: §12 sub-section "The patent-cliff question (part 2 of 3 posed in the brief)"; supporting detail in §4.1 (Brilinta −38%) and §4.3 (Soliris US −28% to $1,092m)
focus_questions.with_what_evidence: Gives a numerical answer — "approximately 15% of revenue (Farxiga) is directly exposed to an LOE that has already begun" ($8,492m global = 14.5% of FY2025 revenue, from the FY2025 Annual Report extract on Form 6-K) and "approximately 23% of revenue sits in the two therapy areas currently in decline" (CVRM $12,764m + V&IT $846m), then converts H1 2026's −12% CVRM / −26% Infectious Disease CER rates into ~$1.5bn + ~$220m annualised, i.e. ~2.9pp of group growth absorbed a year. But the forward half of the question is expressly not answered: the "Method note" concedes "I was unable to extract the per-product expiry years from that document ... I therefore do not state any product's expiry date," so no expiry is actually shown to fall due between Sep 2026 and Sep 2027. And the headline exposure number is global revenue for a US-only event — the table's own right-hand column says "US portion not separately sourced" — for a product that still grew +10% in FY2025 "despite generic competition in some markets." Brilinta's absolute FY2025 sales and Soliris' global total are also unsourced (§18 item 20).

focus_questions.question: Is the oncology pipeline's contribution to growth sourced from approvals and launches, or from assumptions about them?
focus_questions.where: §13 sub-section "The oncology question (part 3 of 3 posed in the brief)"; §4.2 "Oncology in detail (Note 2, FY2025 20-F)"; §12 "Pipeline density is real" and "Named new growth drivers I could source"
focus_questions.with_what_evidence: The note reframes the question as "Is the oncology pipeline's contribution already in the price? On my arithmetic, yes — and then some," and answers that version well: a grid showing only a sustained ~14% oncology CAGR to 2030 lets the rest of the group be flat (−1.9% over five years). On the question as asked it is good on the sourced side — delivered, product-level, region-level revenue with computed 2y CAGRs (Imfinzi +22.8%, Calquence +18.3%, Truqap $6m→$728m, Enhertu combined $4,982m of which AZ books 55.7%), named approvals (Datroway June 2025, Baxfendy US in H1 2026, "43 approvals in major regions" in 2025, "eight first approvals" in H1 2026) — and disciplined about the assumption side: it refuses a third-party "peak sales exceeding $5 billion" tozorakimab figure, saying "that is a third-party projection, not a company figure, and I do not use it in my forecasts." What is missing is the decomposition the question invites: the DCF is a top-down revenue fade (assumption 2: "+6.9%, +5.9%, +5.0%, +4.6%"), with no product-level build, so the note never states what share of its own forecast oncology growth comes from assets already approved and launched versus the ">20 high-value readouts due over the next 18 months." The distinction is acknowledged in prose but never quantified.

focus_questions.question: Does the balance sheet support the dividend and the R&D commitment together through the horizon?
focus_questions.where: §9 "Balance Sheet & Liquidity" ("Assessment" paragraph), §10 "Computed FY2025 owner cash flow, three definitions", §11 "Capital Allocation" ("Assessment")
focus_questions.with_what_evidence: Answered with figures and a clear verdict: net debt $26,912m at 30 Jun 2026 (H1 2026 6-K), 0.534x equity, 1.46x FY2025 Core operating profit, A1/A+ ratings unchanged (6-K Note 3), interest cover 15.9x — "The constraint on AstraZeneca is not solvency; it is that the business consumes cash faster than Core EPS suggests, so incremental deals are increasingly debt-funded." The arithmetic is there to test it: FY2025 OCF $14,575m less capex $3,270m less $3,955m non-capex investing = $7,350m against $4,971m of dividends paid (34.1% of OCF); cover 2.86x Core EPS / 2.06x Reported; Core R&D $13,822m = 23.5% of revenue; a FY2025 sources-and-uses table reconciling to within $702m of the actual net-debt move; and the H1 2026 counter-evidence — net debt +$3,538m in six months "primarily due to dividend payments and deal-related expenses," OCF down $875m, cash tax at 31% of Reported PBT, working capital −$3,588m and a current ratio of 0.89x. Two reservations: the answer is distributed across three sections rather than assembled into one horizon coverage test (the $3.30 FY2026 dividend ≈ $5.1bn is never set against FY2026E FCFE of $8,699m explicitly), and the committed undrawn facility quantum is unsourced (§9, §18 item 20), so headroom is asserted from ratings rather than measured.

verifiability.how_a_figure_is_checked: Two routes, and both work. Stated facts carry an inline URL, mostly primary (SEC Archives, astrazeneca.com, FCA National Storage Mechanism) — open the link and search the line item, e.g. FY2025 Total Revenue $58,739m to the FY2025 results 6-K (a3234s.htm), Oncology $23,698m to the Annual Report extract PDF, net debt $26,912m and the A1/A+ ratings to the H1 2026 6-K Note 3. Computed figures print their own inputs, so they check with arithmetic without leaving the document: TTM Core EPS is shown as "computed: $9.16 − $4.66 + $5.21", EV as "$247,596m + $26,912m", the Core-to-Reported bridge as "computed: $18,478m − $13,743m". Frictions: no page or note number inside the large PDFs (the Annual Report extract and the results presentation are the two most-cited sources and both need in-document searching); §9's entire balance sheet is routed through a secondary source (Dukascopy) the note itself says it distrusts for market data, even though the primary H1 2026 6-K was evidently read for net debt and ratings; and one figure used twice — TTM Reported EPS of $6.74 — never shows its H1 2025 input.
verifiability.figures_checked: I did not browse (read-only brief), so I re-derived the note's own arithmetic from the inputs it prints — roughly forty computations, and they reconcile. Market cap ($159.64 × 1,550.966708m = $247,597m), EV, EV/Sales 4.67x, EV/Core EBIT 14.9x, all four P/E lines, dividend yield 2.07%, FCF yield 4.57%, net debt/equity 0.534x; therapy-area sum $54,601m and the $972m residual; two-year revenue CAGR 13.24%; the $80bn CAGR 6.375%; the H1 growth attribution (46% × 15% = +6.9pp, 36% × −5% = −1.8pp); OCF margins 20.3% H1 2026 vs 25.3% H1 2025; goodwill+intangibles at 117% of equity; the net-debt bridge $24,570m → $23,374m → $26,912m; the FY2025 sources-and-uses residual $1,898m; owner cash flow $7,350m and its 2.97% yield; the 2026 discount factor (1.085^−0.3 = 0.976) and the 50% first-period weight that reconciles the $8,699m FCFE to its $4,244m PV; the terminal value $245,319m and $126.98 per share; the probability weighting 0.25/0.50/0.25 to $132.04 and the −15.2% total return; the oncology CAGR grid ($23,698m × 1.14^5 = $45,633m, rest-of-group −1.9%); Tagrisso/Imfinzi/Calquence/Enhertu 2y CAGRs; the 47.5% payout cross-check. Two things did not reconcile: gross debt $32,239m less cash $4,893m is $27,346m, $434m above the stated $26,912m net debt, unexplained; and the FY2025 P&L table leaves an unlabelled $579m of operating expense in both the Reported and Core columns (R&D + SG&A do not sum to total opex on either basis).

Whether H1 2026's $875m OCF shortfall and the 31%-of-PBT cash tax rate are timing or structural — the note flags this as "the single item in the accounts I would most want management to explain"
The Q3 2026 reporting date, and the committed undrawn bank facility quantum from the going-concern note
What drove the share price from $190.43 (6 July, Form 4) to ~$160 in two months beyond the 9–10% CARDIO-TTRansform fall — the note notices the de-rating but never investigates it
rubric.first_thing_to_check: The reference price itself. Every return figure in the note hangs off $159.64, yet the note also sources $190.43 for the same ordinary share on 6 July 2026 (Form 4, §6 and §18 item 8) and concedes in §17 that HSBC's 13,920 GBp Hold target converts to \"roughly $186\" at the last exchange rate it had — while §3 insists \"the NYSE line is now one ordinary share, not a fractional-ADR.\" Those cannot all be right without a very large sterling move; the note cross-checks far smaller discrepancies obsessively but leaves this one flagged and unresolved. One GBP/USD quote for 10 September 2026 settles it in under a minute, and it tells you whether the headline is −17% or −29%. Second, and cheap from the same 20-F: Farxiga's US share of its $8,492m, because \"approximately 15% of revenue directly exposed\" is a global number attached to a US-only loss of exclusivity, for a product that grew +10% in FY2025.
rubric.strongest_paragraph: §1 Executive Summary, the paragraph beginning \"Reverse-engineered, the market is paying for:\" — \"a cost of equity of 7.20% (at 2.0% terminal growth), or a 3.90% perpetual growth rate (at my 8.5% cost of equity), or a sustained operating cash-flow margin of 30.8% of revenue against 24.8% delivered in FY2025 ($14,575m / $58,739m). Each is achievable; none is conservative.\" It turns a share price into three falsifiable statements, sets each against a delivered actual computed from a sourced filing line, and refuses the easy verdict that they are impossible. §13.5 shows the working and §14.2–14.3 show how much of the grid clears spot (\"Only 6 of 30 cells reach or exceed the current price\"). The mechanism behind it — §1's observation that Core EPS strips out amortisation of acquired IP while \"the cash cost of acquiring that IP recurs, undiminished, every year in investing cash flow\", a $4,735m FY2025 gap — is the note's one real analytical idea, and it is carried consistently into assumption 7 of the DCF rather than left as a rhetorical flourish.
rubric.weakest_paragraph: §12's \"The patent-cliff question\", starting with the \"Method note\": \"I was unable to extract the per-product expiry years from that document within my research budget, and I therefore do not state any product's expiry date.\" This is the brief's first focus question, and it is answered around the missing document rather than with it — no expiry falling inside the horizon is ever identified, and the exposure table's headline, \"$8,492m global, = 14.5% of FY2025 Total Revenue\", is global revenue presented as at risk from a US event, with \"US portion not separately sourced\" in the same cell, for a product that grew +10% in FY2025. The honesty is real but it does not substitute for the number. §14.4's comparables table (ten peers, every cell \"not sourced\", conceded to leave the Underweight \"resting entirely on the DCF and the reverse-DCF\") and §6, a governance section reduced to a disclaimer, are the other two voids; §12 is the one that matters most because a focus question depends on it. The document also ends mid-sentence in the source appendix at \"| 40 | Morning\", and line 1 carries a stray working preamble — \"I'll research AstraZeneca's primary sources before writing. Let me begin.\" — fused into the title.
rubric.overall: This is a usable research note rather than a polished one, and the parts that matter to someone spending their own money are mostly the parts that work. The arithmetic hygiene is unusually good: I re-derived about forty of its computed figures from the inputs it prints and they reconcile, including the DCF's discount factors, terminal value, per-share output and probability weighting. Nearly every claim carries a primary URL, mostly SEC filings and the company's own RNS, and §18 \"Validation & Disagreements\" does something most notes never do — it lists the cross-checks that passed, names four third-party sources whose figures it could not reproduce (Dukascopy's enterprise value, GuruFocus's free cash flow, MarketChameleon's SG&A, Investing.com's London quote) and says which it discarded and why. The thesis is argued, not recited: it is 38% below the consensus target it quotes, and the mechanism it rests on (Core EPS excludes amortisation of acquired IP while the cash cost of acquiring it recurs in investing cash flow) is carried into a specific, sensitised model input rather than left as prose. The bear case, the bull case and the author's own nominated weak point are all numbered and in the body. On the brief, focus question 3 is answered, and 1 and 2 are answered partly — 1 by revealed erosion rather than by any expiry date, 2 in a reframed form that never decomposes forecast oncology growth into launched versus pipeline-dependent. The reservations are substantial and mostly self-declared. The rating is \"one assumption deep\" by the note's own admission: an unsourced 8.5% cost of equity, with a Hold at 7.2%, and no comps cross-check because §14.4 is empty. Two checklist items fail — there is no account of the company's own named risk factors from the FY2025 20-F (and unlike the other gaps, that one is not declared), and management or board changes are absent altogether. Open legal matters amount to one stale Chinese appraisal opinion of unknown current status, with the 20-F legal-proceedings note unread. Competitive position names one competing product. The largest declared hole — US drug pricing, MFN, tariffs, maximum fair prices — falls squarely inside the 90-day window and inside the margin question the valuation turns on. And for all its cross-checking discipline the note leaves a ~16% unresolved gap between two of its own sourced prices for the same ordinary share. A Claude subscription would not, unprompted, produce this depth of filing-level detail or this much self-audit; but it would also let me close the four gaps above in an afternoon, which is what I would do before acting. I would use this as the framework and the arithmetic, and I would not sell or stand aside on the $132 target until the reference price, the Farxiga US split, the 20-F risk and legal sections and a defensible discount rate were settled.

focus_questions.question: How exposed is revenue to the patent expiries falling due inside the horizon?
focus_questions.where: §12 sub-heading "The patent-cliff question (part 2 of 3 posed in the brief)", its four-row exposure table, and the "Answer to the question" paragraph; §18 item 15
focus_questions.with_what_evidence: Strong on exposure already crystallised: Farxiga $8,492m FY2025 global sales = 14.5% of Total Revenue with generic dapagliflozin approved and marketed (H1 2026 6-K naming Farxiga US LOE as a headwind, plus Citeline and Drugs.com); Brilinta −38% CER on US/EU generic entry (FY2025 AR extract); Soliris US −28% to $1,092m on biosimilars (FY2025 20-F); Crestor/Nexium/Pulmicort/Seloken/Synagis/Zoladex named as already off-patent in all major markets (AZ Patent Expiries schedule). It then converts this into a revealed measure: CVRM + Vaccines = 23.2% of revenue, running −12% and −26% CER in H1 2026, sized at ~$1.5bn + ~$220m annualised, "about 2.9 percentage points of group growth". But the question as posed — expiries falling due inside the 12-month horizon — is not answered, and the note says why: "I was unable to extract the per-product expiry years from that document within my research budget, and I therefore do not state any product's expiry date." It declines to date the next wave ("I will not state dates I did not read"). Worse for the headline figure, the Farxiga LOE is a US event but the 14.5% is the global sales number, with "US portion not separately sourced" — so the note's own answer ("approximately 15% of revenue is directly exposed") is on the high side by an unstated margin, and Brilinta's absolute sales are never given at all.

focus_questions.question: Is the oncology pipeline's contribution to growth sourced from approvals and launches, or from assumptions about them?

verifiability.how_a_figure_is_checked: Two routes, and both mostly work. Sourced figures carry an inline hyperlink immediately after the claim, named for the document rather than the host ("FY2025 20-F", "H1 2026 6-K", "Patent Expiries 2025"), with an Appendix that numbers sources and gives publication dates. Computed figures show their inputs at the point of use — the key-metric table in §1 has a dedicated "Inputs" column ($274,508m / $58,739m), and derivations are written out in the text ($9.16 − $4.66 + $5.21 for TTM Core EPS). Three real frictions. First, there are no in-document locators: checking $58,739m means opening a 20-F exhibit and searching, because no page, note or section is given for most claims (§4.2 is a rare exception, labelled "Note 2"). Second, the body uses bare links, not numbered footnotes, so the Appendix's numbering is decorative — you cannot go from a claim to source #4. Third, the file is unfinished at both ends: it opens with a stray line before the title ("I'll research AstraZeneca's primary sources before writing. Let me begin.") and stops mid-row at "| 40 | Morning", so the source list is truncated and the secondary-source section — Dukascopy, GuruFocus, Wallflake, Macrotrends, Citeline, MarketChameleon, all of which the body relies on — never appears in the Appendix at all.
verifiability.figures_checked: I re-derived roughly sixty of the note's computed figures from the inputs it shows, and nearly all reproduce. Market cap $247,596m = $159.64 x 1,550.97m; EV $274,508m and all five multiples in §1; TTM Core EPS $9.71 and 16.4x; the segment table sums to $54,601m with a $972m residual exactly as stated; every regional row in §4.2 sums to its total and all eight two-year CAGRs are right to 0.1pp; the Enhertu 55.7% share; §7.1's growth rates; the $4,735m Core-to-Reported bridge; §8's gap-per-share and conversion ratios; §9's balance sheet balances exactly ($87,868 + $27,965 = $65,463 + $50,370) and BVPS cross-ties to the independently sourced share count; §10's three owner-cash yields and the TTM FCF rebuild of $10,220m; §11's cover, payout and sources-and-uses residual; §12's Farxiga 14.5%, the 23.2% and the 2.9pp drag; the whole of §13.4 — revenue path, margins, capex, BD, FCFE, the 8.5% discount factors including the 0.3-year first period and the 50% FY2026 weight, the $82,063m PV sum, the terminal value and $126.98; both reverse-DCF solves (at Ke 7.20%/g 2.0% I get $159.72 and at Ke 8.5%/g 3.90% I get $159.51 against a $159.64 price); two cells of each sensitivity grid; the bear and bull 2030 revenue figures from their own growth columns; the $132.04 probability weighting and the −15.2% total return; and §18's own cross-checks. Three small things do not reconcile from the text alone. §7.2 shows Reported total operating expense of $34,744m against R&D $14,232m + SG&A $19,933m = $34,165m (the same $579m gap on the Core column), unexplained — presumably distribution costs, but the reader is not told. §9 shows gross debt $32,239m less cash $4,893m = $27,346m against a stated net debt of $26,912m, a $434m difference with no note. And §12 says H2 2026 is "H1 2026's +6% CER plus ~2pp FX", which gives $33.1bn, yet the number used is "≈$32.8bn" (the DCF implies +6.94%); the direction is conservative but the stated method does not produce the stated figure.

rubric.first_thing_to_check: Farxiga's US-only revenue. The note's answer to focus question 1 — "approximately 15% of revenue (Farxiga) is directly exposed to an LOE that has already begun inside the horizon" — applies the $8,492m global sales figure to a United States loss of exclusivity, and the table says so in as many words: "US portion not separately sourced." Since the US is only ~40% of group revenue, the true in-horizon exposure could be a third of the headline, which would materially soften the central thesis. Check that figure in the 20-F's product-by-region revenue note before anything else. Second in line: the 8.5% cost of equity, because the note's own reverse DCF shows 7.20% makes the shares fairly valued, and it concedes "The rating is one assumption deep."
rubric.strongest_paragraph: §13.5 "Reverse DCF — what is priced in", with its closing line "None of these is impossible. All three are optimistic simultaneously against the company's own recent delivery." It converts an opinion into three falsifiable statements about what the buyer at $159.64 must believe — a 7.20% cost of equity, or 3.90% perpetual growth, or a 30.8% terminal OCF margin — and benchmarks each against something sourced: the company's own 4.9% long-dated coupons, and the 24.8% OCF margin delivered in FY2025 versus 20.3% in H1 2026. I reproduced two of the three solves from the note's own forecast table to within $0.20 of the market price, which is the best evidence in the document that its arithmetic is real. §18 "Validation & Disagreements" runs it close: fourteen numbered cross-checks and resolved conflicts, including catching that a secondary source's $190bn market cap implies $122.50 a share when the company's own Form 4 records $190.43 three weeks earlier.
rubric.weakest_paragraph: §6 "Management & Governance". It opens by conceding it is "materially incomplete" and then fills the space with material that is not governance: two months of share-count movement re-labelled as "exceptionally tight share-count management" on a 0.004% dilution, one officer's routine Share Incentive Plan purchase used chiefly to harvest a share price, the mechanics of the NYSE listing harmonisation, and a CDP climate rating. The one substantive governance observation — FY2024 impairments of $753m on vemircopan, $504m on Andexxa and $165m on FPI-2059 read as "a comment on acquisition pricing" — belongs in the earnings-quality section and appears there anyway. Declaring a gap is not the same as covering the item, and this is the only checklist line the note scores nothing on while appearing to address it. §14.4's comparables table runs it close: ten peer rows in which every one of sixty cells reads "not sourced".
rubric.overall: Judged as a document by a reader with only the file, this is unusually trustworthy on the numbers and unusually candid about its holes, but it is not a finished note and it does not answer the brief it was given. The trust case is strong: I re-derived about sixty computed figures from the inputs shown and nearly all reproduce, including the entire ten-year DCF, both reverse-DCF solves to within $0.20 of the market price, the scenario weighting, and a balance sheet that balances to the dollar; sources are named by document with direct links; and §18 volunteers fourteen cross-checks, several of which catch and discard bad third-party data. The discipline about provenance is real — a peak-sales projection is refused because it is a third party's, a stale exchange rate is refused for a currency conversion, a residual is labelled "approximate". Against that, three things would stop me acting on it as written. First, the brief's three questions are not the three the note answers: it labels US drug pricing as "part 1 of 3 posed in the brief", reframes the oncology question from provenance to price, and never assembles a horizon verdict on the dividend and R&D together, so all three focus questions come out partly answered. Second, the central quantification of patent exposure applies a global sales figure to a US expiry by the note's own admission, and it states no expiry dates at all because it could not read the schedule it links — so the question of what falls due inside the horizon is left open. Third, whole checklist items are missing rather than thin: the company's own named risks, any board or management change, and every peer comparison, which the note concedes leaves the rating "entirely on the DCF and the reverse-DCF" and, by its own words, "one assumption deep" on an unsourced 8.5% cost of equity. There is also a verifiability inconsistency the front matter does not admit: §1 promises every number is from a primary filing or computed from one, yet the §9 balance sheet, the interest cover and the working-capital claims come from a secondary aggregator the note elsewhere distrusts. Finally, the file itself is unfinished — a stray sentence sits above the title and the source appendix stops mid-row at entry 40, leaving every secondary source unlisted. I would use the segment analysis, the earnings-quality work and the reverse DCF immediately; I would not take the Underweight to a decision without the Farxiga US split, a peer cross-check, and a defensible discount rate.

The companies named most often (Daiichi Sankyo, Amgen, Merck, Ionis, HUTCHMED) are partners, not competitors, and Beyfortus cannibalising Synagis is AZ against itself. §14.4 names ten peers but every cell reads "not sourced". checklist.item: regulatory or legal matters currently open

checklist.item: a valuation with stated assumptions and a per-share result
checklist.where: §13 "Valuation — Discounted Cash Flow": §13.2 lists twelve numbered assumptions each with a justification and, where possible, a filing citation; §13.4 gives the ten-year FCFE build, $245,319m terminal value, $196,940m equity and "$126.98" per share; §13.5 reverse-DCF; §14.1 probability-weighted "$132.04". checklist.item: a bear case with a number attached
checklist.where: §14.1 "Three scenarios, every input changed explicitly" — bear equity value $109,679m, "$70.72" per share, -55.7% versus spot, 25% probability, with every driver shown (2030 revenue $67,186m or 16% short of the ambition, terminal OCF margin 23.0%, cost of equity 9.0%, BD 4.0% of revenue) and a narrative naming the mechanisms. verifiability.how_a_figure_is_checked: Most facts carry an inline accession-level SEC EDGAR link (FY2025 20-F .../azn-20251231x20f.htm, H1 2026 6-K .../azn-20260630x6k.htm, AR extracts as Ex.99-1 PDFs), and the Appendix lists 40 documents by type and filing date, so you land on the right filing and search the line rather than hunting a site. Computed figures show their own inputs inline — "computed: $9.16 - $4.66 + $5.21", "$274,508m / $18,478m", "$18,478m - $13,743m" — so they recompute with no fetch at all; I reproduced the entire DCF that way. Three routes dead-end: the 30 June 2026 balance sheet resolves only to a Dukascopy page (secondary), H1 2026 Core operating profit of "$10.5bn" carries no citation despite being used twice to justify the 26% terminal margin, and the business description leans on a Yahoo Finance company profile when the 20-F had already been read.
verifiability.figures_checked: I recomputed everything internal and it ties: market cap ($159.64 x 1,550,966,708 = $247,595m), EV $274,508m, EV/sales 4.67x, EV/Core EBIT 14.86x, all four P/Es, TTM Core EPS $9.71, dividend yield 2.07%, FCF yield 4.57%, net debt/equity 0.534x; revenue components summing to $58,739m; the §4.1 therapy-area sum of $54,601m and its $972m residual; every §4.2 regional row summing to its medicine total and every 2-year CAGR (Tagrisso 11.84%, Imfinzi 22.8%, Calquence 18.3%, Enhertu 93.5%); Enhertu economics at 55.7%; the H1 growth decomposition (46% x 15% = +6.9pp, 36% x -5% = -1.8pp); the erosion sizing ($1,532m + $220m = 2.98pp); the $80bn CAGR of 6.38%; the balance sheet ($115,833m both ways), working capital -$3,588m, current 0.886x, quick 0.667x; the net-debt bridge; the Core-to-Reported gap table; owner-cash yields of 5.89/4.57/2.97%; the TTM FCF reconciliation against GuruFocus ($13,700m - $3,480m = $10,220m); and the full DCF — discount factors from 0.976 at 0.3 years to 0.468 at 9.3 years, the PV column, the $82,063m explicit sum, the terminal value, $126.98, the bear and bull revenue paths, and $132.04. Three things fail. (1) Gross debt $32,239m less cash $4,893m = $27,346m, not the $26,912m primary net debt — a $434m gap never addressed. (2) The stated FY2026 revenue build gives $33.1bn for H2 but the table uses $32.8bn, landing on exactly +8.1%. (3) H1 2026 Core operating profit of "$10.5bn" has no source and anchors both the 34.2% Core margin and the 26.0% terminal OCF assumption. The large majority of figures are recomputable or point at a specific filing; what I cannot verify without fetching is whether the primary lines were read correctly in the first place.

rubric.first_thing_to_check: The 8.5% cost of equity in §13.2 assumption 9 and §13.3, which the note itself calls \"an assumption, not a derivation\" built as a 3.6pp spread over AZ's own bond coupons with \"no risk-free rate, equity risk premium, or beta\" sourced. §18 concedes \"The rating is one assumption deep\", and §13.5 shows the market-implied figure is 7.20%, at which the shares are fair — worth roughly $33 per share of the gap to consensus. Build an observable discount rate from AZ's actual bond yields to maturity, a beta and a current risk-free rate before taking the $132 target seriously. Second check: the Farxiga US revenue split, on which the entire answer to focus question 1 rests.
rubric.strongest_paragraph: §13.5 \"Reverse DCF — what is priced in\", with its follow-through in §17. It converts an opinion into three falsifiable market-implied numbers — a 7.20% cost of equity, a 3.90% perpetual growth rate, or a 30.8% terminal operating cash-flow margin — each benchmarked against something the company has actually delivered (4.9% long-dated coupons; 24.8% OCF margin in FY2025 and 20.3% in H1 2026), then concedes \"None of these is impossible\" before arguing they cannot all hold at once. §17 completes the work by attributing the gap to consensus in per-share terms: roughly $22 from charging business development as a cost and roughly $33 from the discount rate. That is a testable disagreement rather than a narrative, and all three implied solves check out against the note's own sensitivity grids.
rubric.weakest_paragraph: §12 \"The patent-cliff question (part 2 of 3 posed in the brief)\". Having correctly disclosed that it could not extract the expiry schedule and would state no expiry date, it then puts a confident headline on the question anyway: \"approximately 15% of revenue (Farxiga) is directly exposed to an LOE that has already begun inside the horizon\". That figure is Farxiga's global FY2025 sales, for a US-only loss of exclusivity that began before the as-of date, on a product that grew +10% in FY2025, with the US portion admitted unsourced — so it is neither the exposure nor the horizon the brief asked about. It is the one place where the note's honesty about a gap does not stop a number being asserted across it. Runner-up: §9, where the whole 30 June 2026 balance sheet is taken from Dukascopy — a source §18 item 8 discards for its market cap, EV and P/E — and the claim that its \"balance-sheet line items ... reconcile to primary sources\" is never demonstrated, while gross debt less cash misses primary net debt by $434m.
rubric.overall: An unusually auditable note, candid about its own holes, but the rating is thinner than 700 lines suggest. Everything checkable internally ties: the DCF reproduces from the stated assumptions (discount factors, $245,319m terminal value, $126.98, the 25/50/25 weighting to $132.04), the therapy-area and medicine-level revenue tables sum to their stated totals, the CAGRs recompute, the net-debt bridge reconciles and the balance sheet balances. Nearly every figure is either an accession-level SEC link or shows its inputs inline, so a reader reaches a source in a couple of minutes for revenue, EPS, cash flow, dividends, share count and ratings. The problems sit at the inputs, not the arithmetic. Focus question 1 is not really answered — no expiry date is stated for any product, so nothing is shown to fall due inside the horizon, and the headline \"15% exposed\" is global sales for a US LOE that began earlier. The rating hangs on an unsourced 8.5% cost of equity that the note itself calls its weakest link, with no comparables cross-check at all (§14.4 is a table of \"not sourced\" cells), so a call 38% below consensus rests on one assumption plus a DCF whose terminal value is 58% of the answer. The 30 June 2026 balance sheet comes from a secondary source the note discards elsewhere, and gross debt less cash misses primary net debt by an unexplained $434m. The company's own principal risks and any board or management change are absent. One load-bearing figure, H1 2026 Core operating profit of \"$10.5bn\", carries no citation and drives the terminal margin. Credit where due: the reverse DCF, the per-share attribution of the consensus gap, and §18's line-by-line record of source conflicts (GuruFocus FCF, MarketChameleon SG&A, Dukascopy EV, vendor EPS spreads) are genuine analytical work rather than confident prose, and the note repeatedly declines to estimate where it could not read. Usable as a fact base and a framework; I would not take the $132 on trust. The file also ends mid-sentence at appendix row 40, so the source list is incomplete as delivered.

verdict.what_A_has_that_B_lacks:
**Provenance machinery B has no equivalent of.** Every fact in A cites a hashed primary artefact (SEC XBRL company facts, the 10-K of 29 July 2026, the 8-K of 2 September 2026) with publisher, publication and retrieval date and tier; every ratio cites its formula and the code version that produced it (e.g. "[^6]: Calculated: `operating margin = operating income / revenue` = 0.4678 ... `aer.calc.ratios:operating_margin`, code version `f17f7158e569`"). B's FY26 balance sheet, by its own admission in §9, is "drawn from secondary aggregators", and its $329.1bn uncommenced-lease plank rests on btw.media [S29] and a Substack [S30].

**A validator record and a point-in-time claim.** "Validation Metrics" reports citation_accuracy 1.00, hallucinated_citation_rate 0, temporal_compliance 1.00, primary_source_ratio 1.00, and the header asserts "Point-in-time: enforced". B has no such attestation.

**An adversarial challenge to its own output.** "Validation & Disagreements" carries six severity-graded red-team entries escalated for human decision, including one at 5/5 attacking A's own headline margins ("recorded ebitda is $97.98bn ... against $194.2bn claimed") and one at 4/5 attacking its own valuation ("the calculation index contains no DCF, no cost of equity or WACC"). B's §18 is self-checking only; nothing challenges B.

**A longer margin history, and an obligation picture B does not build.** Footnotes [^42]–[^56] carry FY2022–FY2026 gross, operating and net margin from XBRL. Balance Sheet & Liquidity makes the point B never makes: "total liabilities of $316.0 billion dwarf funded debt — on any definition that pulls in leases, long-dated tax balances and other accruals, gearing is materially higher than 0.09x", plus the quick-ratio/deferred-revenue caveat and, in the red-team entry, "$28.6bn of non-current accrued income taxes sits outside the net-debt measure entirely".

**Facts B does not have:** the Di Sibio appointment of 13 May 2026 to Audit and Compensation and Reid Hoffman not standing for re-election (Management & Governance); the unresolved IRS Notices of Proposed Adjustment on intercompany transfer pricing, the software-capitalisation/technological-feasibility policy and goodwill DCF testing (Red Flags); and power, grid capacity, land, zoning and permitting as "the binding constraint is physical" (Growth Outlook) — B never mentions power.

**Candour in the DCF caveats:** terminal value is 79.4% (Gordon) and 88.9% (exit multiple) of EV, and "Book equity was used as the equity weight ... so the equity weight is understated, the debt weight overstated, and the resulting WACC too low. Every valuation discounted at it is correspondingly too high."
verdict.what_B_has_that_A_lacks:
**A decision.** "UNDERWEIGHT | Target price $405 | Last close $493.16 | 12-month horizon", with expected total return "−17.1%". A's header says "Non-binding view: no view reached" and A never states a share price or market capitalisation anywhere, so its value-per-share figures cannot be compared to anything.

**Segment dollars, which A says do not exist.** §4 gives FY25 and FY26 revenue, cost of revenue, opex and operating income for all three segments plus a year-on-year bridge: Intelligent Cloud gross margin 62.2% → 58.0%, "−420bp", driven by "segment cost of revenue grew 44.1% against revenue growth of 29.7%", with Microsoft Cloud gross margin 69% (FY25) → 68/67/66 through FY26 quarters. A's Segment Analysis states "no segment-level dollar figures ... were available to cite here".

**The decomposition that answers question 1.** §8 rejects the premise — "cloud margin is not expanding" — then decomposes the +116bp of group operating margin into gross margin −88bp and opex/revenue +204bp, concluding "every basis point of that came from operating-expense leverage" and "opex leverage of this magnitude is not repeatable".

**The capitalisation sizing A declines to attempt.** $115.95bn of capex against roughly $24–44bn charged, "a $72bn to $92bn per year of economic cost not yet in the P&L", with an explicit "that is not the right accounting ... but it is the right *magnitude check*". A's Earnings Quality calls useful lives "unverifiable" and declines to estimate.

**The useful-life change A does not know happened.** Lives extended "from 15 to 25 years" effective FY27, disclosed alongside the calendar-2026 capex guide cut "from approximately $190bn to approximately $175bn" purely from reclassifying finance leases as operating leases — "$15bn of spending moved accounting bucket, not existence" — and the observation that operating-lease payments sit inside operating cash flow, so FCF is roughly unchanged while the capex headline improves.

**The actual free cash flow trajectory.** §10: FY25 $71.6bn → FY26 $66.99bn, "−6.4%"; FCF margin 25.4% → 20.2%; capex 22.9% → 34.9% of revenue; FCF conversion of operating income 55.7% → 43.2%; Q4 FCF "$19.64bn, down 23%". A's "At a glance" instead labels $139,225m "Free cash flow" (a model FCFF per footnote [^8]) and never states operating cash flow less capex in dollars.

**Reverse-engineering the price.** §13.5: implied WACC 7.94%, implied perpetual growth 5.78%, required steady-state FCF "$250bn — 3.7x FY26"; FCF yield 1.84% against a 4.95% 10-year Treasury; and the framing "**The market is paying the bull case**" ($488 bull vs $493.16).

**Forward-demand evidence absent from A:** commercial RPO "$678bn, up 84%" set against "bookings ex-OpenAI up 18%" and the concentration inference drawn from the gap; Azure past $100bn; Copilot ">30 million paid seats" plus usage-based billing; the FY27 guidance table (Q1 revenue $89.85–90.95bn, Azure ~+45% cc, Windows OEM and Devices "decline high teens"); an FY27 EPS estimate of ~$19.19.

**Non-operating marks:** "+$4,963m / +$0.67 EPS" OpenAI gain versus "−$3,620m / −$0.49" in FY25, the "$3.2bn gain on the Anthropic investment", and ex-OpenAI EPS of $17.28 at 28.5x.

**Scenario and sensitivity output:** bear/base/bull at $186/$341/$488 with 25/50/25 probabilities, a 30-cell WACC × terminal-growth grid ("Only one of thirty cells ... exceeds the current price"), a second grid on cash margin × capital intensity, a dated catalyst calendar (Q1 FY27 late October, annual meeting 8 December 2026), and the consensus comparison ("Strong Buy", $572.92 average target). A's Scenarios section says "None of these swings can be sized"; its Catalysts section says no dated forward event exists; its comps section says "every one of the eight proposed peers was excluded".

**Internal cross-checking:** §18.1 ties segment revenue and operating income to the group total, recomputes non-GAAP growth to +22.1% against the disclosed +22%, and reconciles capex two ways to $115.948bn / $116.0bn.
verdict.which_would_you_hand_to_a_colleague_and_:
**B, with A attached as the audit companion — but B is the one that supports a decision.**

B answers all three questions with numbers and, on the first, corrects the question: the note shows cloud margin contracting (Intelligent Cloud 62.2% → 58.0%), shows that the whole +116bp of group operating margin came from opex leverage rather than cloud economics, and then sizes the capitalisation effect A explicitly declines to size. On the second it is honest that no AI revenue line exists, shows its inference working (Microsoft Cloud contributed $45.6bn of $50.1bn of FY26 growth; Azure ~$29bn), and answers the "if it does not" half with the FCF path and a reverse DCF. On the third it gives the quarterly operating-margin walk 48.9 → 47.1 → 46.3 → 45.1 — "the single most important line in this note", and the Q4 exit rate is below the FY25 full-year average — and lands on a falsifiable 12-month conclusion against a stated close.

Three caveats I would pass on with it. Verify the 30 June 2026 balance sheet and the $329.1bn uncommenced-lease figure against the 10-K before relying on either; B flags both itself ("This is the weakest-sourced part of the note"), and the lease number carries a thesis pillar and a risk on a blog and a Substack. The ERP of 5.0% and beta of 1.00 are the author's own assumptions, labelled as such, and §13.5 shows the conclusion turns on them. And the case is substantially a rate call — "the largest single driver of the multiple" is the 10-year at 4.95% — which a reader who disagrees about rates should discount accordingly.

A is the better artefact for tracing a number to its source and the only one of the two that red-teams itself, and its Balance Sheet section is sharper than B's on funded-versus-total obligations. But I could not act on it. It reaches no view by design, quotes no share price, misses the 15-to-25-year useful-life change that is central to question one, and carries three irreconcilable headline figures: "Free cash flow $139,225m" against a Cash Flow section that never states operating cash flow less capex; "Value per share (base) $485.29" against $242.78 (Gordon) and $449.79 (exit multiple) in the DCF section and a sensitivity grid whose 25 footnoted cells run $196–$318. Its own executive summary says "No discounted cash flow, cost of equity, weighted average cost of capital, terminal value, value per share or peer multiple sits on this record" while §Valuation shows all of them, and its red team says the headline margins the thesis leans on in eight sections do not reconcile to the calculation record — unresolved, "escalated for human decision". A reader with money at stake is told, by the document itself, not to trust its headline numbers.

verdict.which_would_you_hand_to_a_colleague_and_:
**B, with two written cautions.** B answers the brief as posed; A declines to.

On the focus questions the gap is not close.
