B reframes Q1 correctly and proves it from segment arithmetic a reader can redo by hand ("The premise is wrong: cloud margin is not expanding" — IC gross margin −420bp, cost of revenue +44.1% on revenue +29.7%), then quantifies the capitalisation flattery ($72–92bn/yr not yet in the P&L). A's Segment Analysis concedes it cannot establish cloud margin at all, and its Earnings Quality section, having correctly identified that "The live earnings-quality question is capitalisation, not accruals", then declines to size it. On Q3, B gives the decomposition (+204bp opex, −88bp gross), the exit rate below the FY25 average, an FY27E and a target; A gives "no view reached" and no share price, so there is no 12-month view in the document.

The decisive problem with A is that it contradicts itself on the one thing a research note exists to deliver. The Executive Summary says "No discounted cash flow, cost of equity, weighted average cost of capital, terminal value, value per share or peer multiple sits on this record", and the Investment Thesis repeats it — yet "At a glance" prints "WACC | — | 9.3%" and "Value per share (base) | — | $485.29", and the "Valuation — Discounted Cash Flow" section runs a full model with a 9.3% WACC and per-share outputs of $242.78 and $449.79. The $485.29 headline appears nowhere in that section and is double the Gordon result; its footnote [^11] is just another `value_per_share` calculation. A's own red team flags exactly this at severity 4/5 ("the calculation index contains no DCF … The draft's own executive summary concedes there is no valuation output"), and the resolution given for all six objections is "Escalated for human decision at approval". A document that tells me its headline margins are "unreconciled" at severity 5/5 and then leaves it unresolved is not one I can pass on.

A's footnotes also do not survive being followed. Every fact citation — [^1] through [^4], [^12]–[^15], [^26], [^63], [^72] — resolves to the same URL, the whole `companyfacts/CIK0000789019.json` endpoint, with no element name or period, so $331,839m cannot be located. Worse, [^137]–[^141], the evidence for the red-team section, are explicitly "for FY2022" calculations ("current ratio … = 1.7846 … for FY2022", "NOPAT … for FY2022") cited against FY2026 claims, and [^100] cites a `value_per_share` calculation to evidence a share count of 7,453,000,000. So A's provenance apparatus is better *in kind* — hashes, formulas, code versions, tiers, point-in-time — while B's is better *in practice*: nearly every B figure is reproducible from the tables it prints (I checked the segment sums, the margin deltas, the opex decomposition, the Azure and Microsoft Cloud back-solves, and the quarterly margins; all tie), and every line is marked sourced, "my calculation" or "my assumption".

The two cautions I would write on B. First, §9 is built on aggregators — "The 30 June 2026 balance sheet figures below are therefore drawn from secondary aggregators … and should be verified against the 10-K before use" — and it cannot reconcile finance leases ($62bn implied vs Yahoo's $16.53bn). To its credit it says so in §18.2 ("This is the weakest-sourced part of the note") and A's XBRL figures would settle several of those cells, which is the one place A is the better reference. Second, the load-bearing cost-of-capital inputs are asserted: ERP 5.0% and beta 1.00 are both labelled "**This is my assumption, not a sourced figure**", and since the whole conclusion is a discount-rate argument, that is the weak joint — mitigated by the ERP 4.0–5.5% ladder and the 30-cell grid, but a reader should know the target moves $315–$407 on that one choice. I would also mark one arithmetic slip: the "expensed as incurred" check states "155.237 − (115.95 − 44.1)" but reports "$63bn"; the printed formula gives $83bn, and $63bn only follows from the $24bn depreciation figure. It is flagged as a magnitude check, not accounting, so it does not move the argument — but the formula as written does not reproduce the number.

Net: I would hand over B as the note and keep A alongside as the audited fact base for the FY26 income statement, cash flow and balance sheet, where its hashed, formula-level record is genuinely the better reference. I would not circulate A as a research note, because it says three times that it has no valuation and then prints one.

verdict.what_A_has_that_B_lacks:
A has the better provenance architecture and the better source tier. Every fact footnote resolves to SEC XBRL companyfacts or the FY26 10-K/8-K with publisher, publication and retrieval dates, a T1_REGULATORY tier and an artefact hash ("Sources" table: `f8aae2965b20`, `4bcf2da2871a`); every ratio footnote carries the formula and a code version (`aer.calc.ratios:operating_margin`, code version `f17f7158e569`). B has nothing equivalent: its load-bearing balance sheet comes from Yahoo and a blog, and it says so.

A also uniquely has: an assumption provenance ledger naming who proposed and who confirmed each DCF input ("Cost of Capital" and "Forecast Assumptions" tables — "proposed by aer.services.assumption_proposals … confirmed by the operator at the assumptions gate"); four genuinely sharp "Recorded Caveats" (book-value equity weight means "the equity weight is understated … and the resulting WACC too low. Every valuation discounted at it is correspondingly too high"; ">three quarters of the enterprise value is terminal value"; the two terminal methods' spread as "the honest width of the answer"; EV→equity bridge is net debt alone); XBRL-sourced balance-sheet detail B could not get (lease liabilities $16,532m, total liabilities $315,989m, quick ratio 0.93, and in the disagreements log a $46.1bn DebtInstrumentCarryingAmount and $28.6bn of non-current accrued income taxes); the qualification that "total liabilities of $316.0 billion dwarf funded debt — on any definition that pulls in leases … gearing is materially higher than 0.09x"; dated 8-K board events B lacks (Di Sibio appointed 13 May 2026 to Audit and Compensation; Reid Hoffman not standing for re-election); explicit "(surfaced here; unverified)" tags on five of seven risks; a licensed-data redistribution determination; a validation metrics table; and a red-team disagreements log that publishes six unresolved challenges against its own numbers.
verdict.what_B_has_that_A_lacks:
B has the analysis. On focus question 1 it rejects the premise and shows why: "Intelligent Cloud gross margin fell 419bp to 58.0%" because "segment cost of revenue grew 44.1% against revenue growth of 29.7%" (§4 tables, FY25 and FY26 segment P&Ls side by side), Microsoft Cloud gross margin percentage "68% in Q1, 67% in Q2 and 66% in Q3 … versus 69% for FY25", and a decomposition table in §8: gross margin −88bp, opex/revenue +204bp, net +116bp — "every basis point of that came from operating-expense leverage". Then the capitalisation check: $115.95bn of capex against "$24bn and $44bn" charged, "The gap is $72bn to $92bn per year of economic cost not yet in the P&L." Then the useful-life change (15→25 years) and the mechanism A never sees — the finance-to-operating-lease shift cut guided capex "$190bn to approximately $175bn" while operating-lease payments sit inside operating cash flow, so "$15bn of spending moved accounting bucket, not existence."

On question 2: FY25 FCF $71.6bn → FY26 $66.99bn, "Free cash flow fell 6.4% in a year when operating income rose 21%"; Q4 FCF "$19.64bn fell 23%"; capex 34.9% of revenue; a ten-year FCF path (§13.4); a bear case reaching only $153bn of FY36 FCF; and a second sensitivity grid on OCF margin × capital intensity (§14.3) — which is precisely "what the FCF trajectory looks like if it does not". Plus the AI-return question answered with labelled inference: Microsoft Cloud "$45.6bn of the $50.1bn of total FY26 revenue growth — 91%", Azure ~$29.1bn, while refusing a dollar AI-revenue figure.

On question 3: the exit-rate argument A never makes — quarterly operating margin 48.9% → 47.1% → 46.3% → 45.1%, "The full-year average of 46.78% is above FY25's 45.62% … The exit rate reads as compression"; opex +7.4% vs revenue +17.8% and "Opex leverage of this magnitude is not repeatable"; 2 points of FX.

Also uniquely in B: the price ($493.16), market cap, 27.5x P/E, 54.4x EV/FCF and a 1.84% FCF yield against a 4.95% 10-year; a reverse DCF (implied WACC 7.94%, implied perpetual growth 5.78%, required steady-state FCF ~$250bn); three probability-weighted scenarios and a 30-cell WACC × g grid; the RPO concentration point ("$678bn, up 84%" against "bookings grew 18% excluding … OpenAI"); $329.1bn of leases not yet commenced; the "$22.2 billion increase in cash used in other investing … to facilitate the purchase of components"; dated catalysts including the 8 December 2026 AGM A said it could not find; a consensus comparison; an internal-consistency tie-out table (§18.1) where segments sum to $331,839m and capex reconciles two ways to $115.948bn; and a rating, target and expected return — Underweight, $405, −17.1%.
verdict.which_would_you_hand_to_a_colleague_and_:
B, with a written health warning. It is the only one of the two that answers the brief: A's header says "Non-binding view: no view reached", and its Executive Summary says "we take no view on whether the 11 September 2026 share price is fair" — for a note asked for a 12-month view, that is a non-delivery, and A never states the price, the market cap or a single multiple.

A's deeper problem is that it contradicts itself on exactly the load-bearing points. Its thesis says the record "holds no valuation output, no discount rate and no peer multiple", and its own disagreements log repeats that "the calculation index contains no DCF, no cost of equity or WACC, no terminal value and no per-share output" — yet the Valuation section prints a 9.3% WACC, two terminal methods ($242.78 and $449.79) and a 25-cell heatmap, all cited to calculations [^90]–[^133]. Its Key Risks claim "no prior-period comparatives sit here to test durability" while footnotes [^42]–[^56] record gross, operating and net margin for FY2022–FY2026 — the very series needed for questions 1 and 3, held and unused. Its Key Risks say operating cash flow "is not among the figures available here" while six other sections cite $182.9bn. And the "At a glance" headline "Value per share (base) $485.29" reconciles to neither terminal method and appears to be the top of the football-field range ([^101] $207.18, [^102] $485.29) relabelled "base"; "Free cash flow $139,225m" carries no period and no inputs, and cannot be an FY26 figure on A's own NOPAT, D&A and capex. Meanwhile its validators escalated six severity 3–5 challenges — including "Every headline margin the thesis leans on is unreconciled" — unresolved, and the footnotes show that challenge itself is drawn from FY2022 records ([^139] operating margin 0.4206 FY2022; [^141] NOPAT $72.4bn FY2022). Either way the reader is left unable to tell whether A's headline margins are right.

B's faults are real but bounded and mostly disclosed. Tell the colleague to fix or verify four things: (1) §8's magnitude check states "my calculation: 155.237 − (115.95 − 44.1)" and then reports "$63bn … roughly 19%" — that formula gives $83.4bn and 25%; the $63bn corresponds to the $24bn depreciation figure, so the working is mislabelled; (2) the $24–44bn depreciation range is built from a nine-month accumulated-depreciation change (ignores retirements) and Q4 "depreciation, amortisation and other non-cash charges" annualised — A's data imply real FY26 D&A of about $39bn (EBITDA $194.2bn less EBIT $155.2bn), so B's low end is wrong and it drives the headline "$72bn to $92bn"; (3) the $329.1bn uncommenced-lease figure — used for "0.99x FY26 revenue", "74% of book equity" and "net debt/equity ~0.70x" — rests on btw.media and a Substack, not the 10-K commitments note, and is not flagged as weak even though the balance sheet is; (4) B's "~$62bn" finance leases derived from a common-size percentage is almost certainly wrong — A's XBRL figure of $16,532m matches the Yahoo number B could not reconcile. Also note that B's target is set at the favourable end of its own range ($405 at 8.87% WACC) rather than its central $341, for a disclosed presentational reason.

Keep A alongside as the source of record for the FY26 balance sheet and lease liabilities, for the caveat language on terminal-value share and book-value WACC, and for the two board 8-K events. But the note that does the work is B.

verdict.what_A_has_that_B_lacks:
**An answer to each focus question, with arithmetic.**

Q1 (patent expiries in the horizon). A's §12 subsection "The patent-cliff question" sizes it: Farxiga at "$8,492m global, = 14.5% of FY2025 Total Revenue", Brilinta "decreased by 38% (CER: 38%) driven by generic entry in the US and Europe in the first half of 2025", Soliris US "−28% to $1,092m", and the off-patent legacy list (Crestor, Nexium, Pulmicort, Seloken, Synagis, Zoladex). It then does the thing that matters for a 12-month horizon — measures erosion that is already running: CVRM at −12% CER and Infectious Disease at −26% CER applied to the FY2025 base, "roughly a $1.5bn annualised revenue loss… together about 2.9 percentage points of group growth." B's "Segment Analysis" states the opposite conclusion: "the underlying patent expiry dates, US regulatory exclusivity periods, and ex-US supplementary protection certificate or data-exclusivity dates for individual products were not present in the material reviewed," and "any single product line's US-specific exposure to patent expiry… cannot be quantified." Nothing is sized anywhere in B.

Q2 (oncology: approvals/launches or assumptions). A separates the two ledgers explicitly. Realised: §4.2's Note 2 table with Tagrisso $7,254m, Imfinzi $6,063m (2y CAGR +22.8%), Calquence $3,518m (+18.3%), Truqap $6m→$728m, Enhertu combined $4,982m with AstraZeneca booking "55.7% of the combined Enhertu figure (computed)"; §2 attributes "+6.9 percentage points of group CER growth" to oncology against BioPharmaceuticals' "−1.8 points", i.e. "oncology accounted for more than the entirety of group growth in the half." Assumed: the §13.5/oncology-question grid showing "Only at a sustained ~14% oncology CAGR does the rest of the group get to be flat," and the discipline of refusing a third-party number — tozorakimab's "projected peak sales exceeding $5 billion" is labelled "a third-party projection, not a company figure, and I do not use it in my forecasts." B's "Growth Outlook" concedes the reverse: "Asset-level late-stage disclosure — indication, phase, registry record and first plausible revenue period for each registrational programme — is not available… no management revenue ambition can be quoted verbatim," and its base case is "a judgement drawn from financial structure alone."

Q3 (dividend and R&D together). A's §11 gives the cover: dividends paid "$4,971m equal 34.1% of FY2025 OCF", cover "2.86x on Core EPS", R&D "23.5% of revenue", and then the §10 three-definition owner-cash table (OCF $14,575m / less capex $11,305m / less non-capex investing $7,350m) which is what actually decides whether both are affordable. §9 closes it: "The constraint on AstraZeneca is not solvency; it is that the business consumes cash faster than Core EPS suggests, so incremental deals are increasingly debt-funded — as H1 2026's $3,538m net-debt build demonstrates." B's "Cash Flow Analysis" cannot get there: "there is no separate capital expenditure line, no working capital detail… Free cash flow and the durability of conversion therefore cannot be quantified."

**A price, a view and a falsifiable valuation.** Reference price $159.64, target $132, rating Underweight; a full FCFE build (§13.4) whose PV column I checked sums to the stated $82,063m and divides to the stated $126.98; a twelve-row assumption table each with a source; a reverse DCF (§13.5) naming what the market is paying for — "cost of equity of 7.20%… or a 3.90% perpetual growth rate… or a sustained operating cash-flow margin of 30.8%"; two 30-cell sensitivity grids ("Only 6 of 30 cells reach or exceed the current price"); bear/base/bull at $70.72/$126.98/$203.48 with every input changed explicitly. B's "Valuation — Discounted Cash Flow" is a single boxed refusal, and its "Non-binding view" field reads "no view reached."

**The last twelve months of company news.** A has H1 2026 results (revenue $30,672m, Core EPS $5.21, Q2 CER +5%), reconfirmed FY2026 guidance, the $80bn 2030 ambition, the 9 July 2026 CARDIO-TTRansform failure and the ~9–10% share reaction, the Farxiga US LOE, the CSPC/Dizal/Sino Biopharmaceutical upfronts, and the February 2026 NYSE listing harmonisation. B states plainly in "Key Points" that "the latest interim period is Q2 2025 — several quarters behind this note's September 2026 as-of date"; none of the above appears in it.

**Named disagreement with the outside world.** §17 tabulates consensus $212.54, HSBC 13,920 GBp Hold, Berenberg Buy, RBC Buy, GF Value $180.33, and then decomposes its own 38% gap into business development treated as cost ("on the order of $22/share"), cost of equity ("roughly $33/share") and terminal growth. B's "Prior Research Comparison" is one sentence: "This is the first research run."

**Resolved source conflicts rather than escalated ones.** §18 runs 14 numbered cross-checks and resolutions — discarding Dukascopy's enterprise value because "a $190bn market cap over 1,550m shares implies $122.5 per share" against a Form 4-recorded $190.43; rejecting GuruFocus's $6,044m TTM FCF because it cannot be rebuilt from the filings; choosing the company's 26% SG&A over MarketChameleon's 29%; reconciling the net-debt bridge "$24,570m − $1,196m = $23,374m; + $3,538m = $26,912m… All three sources reconcile exactly."

**Dated forward catalysts.** §16 lists Q3 2026 results and the H2 gross-margin guide, the Dizal close, ">20 high-value readouts", tozorakimab's FDA priority review, oral PCSK9 data in H1 2027, and the FY2026 results as "the cleanest test of the patent-cliff thesis." B's "Catalysts" is stamped "Insufficient evidence… its claims cite 0."
verdict.what_B_has_that_A_lacks:
**Three post-H1 primary filings A does not have in primary form.** The 8 September 2026 "ETCAMAH APPROVED IN THE US FOR HR+ BREAST CANCER" release and the 8 September 2026 "IMFINZI+IMDELLTRA IMPROVED OS IN SMALL CELL LUNG" release, both cited to sec.gov with artefact hashes `7e8bf77c81a6` and `b94fd6dd5178`, plus the 1 September 2026 "ADMISSION TO TRADING — EUR2.55 BILLION BOND OFFERING". A names Etcamah nowhere, has the SCLC readout only via a "Robinhood news digest" and "stockanalysis digest" in §16, and misses the euro bond entirely — a live financing event inside the horizon that bears directly on focus question 3.

**Mechanical citation provenance.** Every figure in B carries a footnote that is either a tiered artefact (T1_REGULATORY, with published and retrieved dates and a content hash in the Sources table) or a named calculation with formula, value, period, module and code version — e.g. "`net debt to EBITDA = net debt / EBITDA` = 1.2699… (`aer.calc.ratios:net_debt_to_ebitda`, code version `6d9c6c80d78a`)". A's equivalent discipline is narrative: it says which figures are "computed" and shows inputs, but nothing is hash-anchored and a meaningful minority of its citations are transient aggregator pages (Dukascopy, GuruFocus, Wallflake, CNN, Robinhood, stockanalysis, MarketChameleon, TradingView).

**A longer reported series and some balance-sheet lines A lacks.** Revenue FY2021–FY2025 ($37,417m → $58,739m) against A's three years, with per-year gross, operating and net margin calculations for each of the five years. And from XBRL at 31 December 2025: accounts payable $25,280m, lease liabilities $1,421m, short-term investments $30m ($50m at the half year), cash $5,711m against $7,058m at 30 June 2025, total assets $114,074m. A's equivalent balance-sheet table (§9) is at 30 June 2026 but sourced to "Dukascopy summary… a secondary source" — the aggregator A itself says elsewhere it distrusts.

**An adversarial register with severities.** B's "Validation & Disagreements" carries a validator metric table (citation_accuracy 1.00, primary_source_ratio 1.00, temporal_compliance 1.00, plus two "not exercised") and nine scored red-team findings — including severity 5/5 against its own profitability core and 5/5 against its own balance-sheet conclusion — each with a "Basis" and a resolution status. A's §18 is honest but self-administered; it has no adversarial pass scoring its own conclusions against a recorded calculation register.

**Sharper refusal discipline in one place.** B's "Segment Analysis" declines a specific temptation A partly yields to: "apportioning worldwide product revenue by a group-level regional ratio would manufacture a figure not actually reported and is avoided here." A residualises Rare Disease at "$5.4bn (residual, computed)" and a "$972m residual" of unallocated medicines — both labelled, but both constructed.

**Working-capital classification detail.** B's "Cash Flow Analysis" records the group's stated policy placing EBT share purchases in financing, share-plan taxes in operating, and Alexion replacement awards in investing — "classification choices that shift modest amounts across the three headings and are worth noting when comparing conversion ratios with peers." A notes EBT purchases but not the classification policy.
verdict.which_would_you_hand_to_a_colleague_and_:
Document A, with three caveats attached.

The test is whether the note changes what I do with my money. A does: it gives me a price ($159.64), a target ($132), a rating, and — more usefully than the rating — a reverse DCF that tells me exactly what I have to believe to justify the market price ("a cost of equity of 7.20%… or a 3.90% perpetual growth rate… or a sustained operating cash-flow margin of 30.8% against 24.8% delivered in FY2025"). Those are three assumptions I can hold up against my own view and disagree with precisely. It also answers all three focus questions in dedicated, labelled subsections with sourced numerators and denominators, and where it cannot answer it draws the boundary in the right place: on patent expiries it refuses to state dates it did not read but substitutes revealed erosion ("−12% CVRM run-rate is roughly a $1.5bn annualised revenue loss"), which for a 12-month horizon is the better evidence anyway.

I checked A's arithmetic where it is load-bearing and it holds: the PV column in §13.4 sums to the stated $82,063m, terminal plus explicit gives the stated $196,940m, and $196,940m ÷ 1,550.97m gives the stated $126.98. The net-debt bridge ties. The payout-ratio cross-check reproduces. That is the property I need from a note I am going to act on.

Document B is the more rigorous artefact and the less useful document. Its provenance machinery is genuinely better — hashed artefacts, tiered sources, formula-and-code-version calculation records, a scored red-team pass. But it reaches "no view reached", produces no DCF, no price, no share count, no multiple, no product revenue, no patent schedule, no dated catalyst, and no peer. Its own "Key Points" concede the financial record stops at FY2025 with "the latest interim period… Q2 2025", so the entire year that contains the Farxiga LOE, the H1 2026 deceleration to +5% CER in Q2, the CARDIO-TTRansform failure and FY2026 guidance is simply absent. Worse for verifiability specifically: B publishes 81.9% / 23.4% / 17.4% in a dozen places while its own register says at severity 5/5 that "no calculation in the index reproduces the claimed values", and publishes net income $10,225m and OCF $14,575m next to a finding that the stored facts are $12,402m and $18,736m — nine findings, all "Escalated for human decision at approval", none resolved. (The red team looks to me to be comparing FY2025 claims against FY2021/FY2022 calculations — footnotes 107, 109 and 110 are FY2021 and FY2022 ratios — which is a defect in the challenge rather than in the figures, but B does not say so, and a reader cannot tell which of the two is broken.) A document that cannot vouch for its own headline margins is not one I can lean on, however clean the chain of custody.

The caveats I would pass on with A. First, its rating is one assumption deep and it says so: "If the correct cost of equity for this company today is 7.2% rather than 8.5%, the stock is fairly valued and the rating should be Hold." I would read the note for the decomposition, not the $132. Second, its 30 June 2026 balance-sheet table is sourced to Dukascopy, an aggregator it discredits three sections later — those line items need re-pulling from the H1 2026 statements before anyone relies on the 0.89x current ratio or the −$3,588m working capital. Third, the two acknowledged holes — no peer multiples ("my Underweight rests entirely on the DCF and the reverse-DCF") and no primary source on MFN, Section 232 or maximum fair prices — are exactly the two that could move the conclusion, and B does not fill either. From B I would lift the three September 2026 filings, the euro bond in particular, and staple them to A.

verdict.what_A_has_that_B_lacks:
**A quantified answer to focus question 1.** A's "The patent-cliff question" (in §12 Growth Outlook) tabulates the in-horizon LOEs with evidence: Farxiga at "**$8,492m global**, = **14.5% of FY2025 Total Revenue**" with FDA generic dapagliflozin approvals cited; Brilinta "−38% (CER: 38%) driven by generic entry in the US and Europe in the first half of 2025"; Soliris US "−28% to $1,092m"; and the off-patent legacy list (Crestor, Nexium, Pulmicort, Seloken, Synagis, Zoladex). It then adds a *revealed*-erosion measure — CVRM −12% CER and Infectious Disease −26% CER applied to the FY2025 base, "roughly a **$1.5bn annualised revenue loss**... about **2.9 percentage points of group growth**." B has nothing: Segment Analysis states "the underlying patent expiry dates, US regulatory exclusivity periods, and ex-US supplementary protection certificate or data-exclusivity dates for individual products were not present in the material reviewed," and Scenarios repeats "It does not identify the products facing loss of exclusivity." No product is named in B.

**An answer to focus question 2 that separates delivered from assumed.** A's §2 pillar 1 attributes H1 2026 growth arithmetically — Oncology "+6.9 percentage points" against BioPharmaceuticals "−1.8 points", concluding "oncology accounted for *more than the entirety* of group growth in the half." §4.2 gives medicine-level FY2023–25 revenue and computed 2-year CAGRs (Imfinzi +22.8%, Calquence +18.3%, Enhertu +93.5%, Truqap $6m→$728m). It then separates booked launch revenue (Datroway: "$2m of FY2025 Product Sales and $77m of Alliance Revenue"; Baxfendy "US-approved in H1 2026") from pure assumption (tozorakimab, elecoglipron, "oral PCSK9 with data in H1 2027"), and explicitly refuses a third-party number: "that is a third-party projection, not a company figure, and I do not use it in my forecasts." The oncology-CAGR grid in §13 ("Only at a sustained ~14% oncology CAGR does the rest of the group get to be flat") makes the assumption load explicit.

**An answer to focus question 3 with the two claims set against one cash flow.** §11 Capital Allocation's sources-and-uses table puts OCF $14,575m against capex $3,270m, other investing $3,955m, dividends $4,971m and EBT purchases $521m; dividend cover "2.86x on Core EPS, 2.06x on Reported EPS"; dividends "34.1% of FY2025 OCF"; R&D "23.5% of revenue". §9 tracks net debt $23,374m (31 Dec 2025) → $26,912m (30 Jun 2026), management attributing the rise "primarily due to dividend payments and deal-related expenses," and concludes "the constraint on AstraZeneca is not solvency; it is that the business consumes cash faster than Core EPS suggests."

**A view and the arithmetic behind it.** Rating, reference price ($159.64), target ($132), a full equity DCF with twelve numbered assumptions each justified (§13.2), a ten-year forecast table, a reverse DCF (implied Ke 7.20%, g 3.90%, terminal OCF margin 30.8%), two 30-cell sensitivity grids, and three probability-weighted scenarios ($70.72 / $126.98 / $203.48). B's Valuation section is a refusal: "No discounted cash flow was produced... The valuation needs a share count for the year ending 31 December 2025 and the filings carry none."

**All of FY2026.** H1 2026 revenue $30,672m, Q2 CER "+5%", FY2026 guidance reconfirmed 27 July 2026, the $80bn 2030 ambition and its computed 6.38% CAGR, the H1 2026 cash deterioration (OCF $6,224m vs $7,099m; OCF/revenue 25.3%→20.3%), the cash-tax anomaly ("31% of Reported profit before tax, against a Reported effective tax rate of 17%"), the CARDIO-TTRansform failure of 9 July 2026, and the NYSE listing harmonisation.

**Source adjudication.** §18 records 14 cross-checks and resolutions — the net-debt bridge reconciling "exactly", the payout ratio reproducing "as $3.20 ÷ my computed TTM Reported EPS of $6.74", Dukascopy's EV discarded, GuruFocus FCF "cannot be reproduced", MarketChameleon's 29% SG&A rejected in favour of the company's 26%.

**Consensus context:** "$212.54" consensus target, HSBC/Berenberg/RBC actions, and a line-by-line decomposition of the 38% gap.
verdict.what_B_has_that_A_lacks:
**Provenance machinery A has no analogue for.** Every figure in B carries a footnote naming publisher, publication date, retrieval date and source tier, and the Sources table adds an artefact identifier per document (`f8ee3de56da6` for the XBRL facts, `5f65a1e4d20e` for the 20-F). Every derived number carries its formula, full-precision value, period and code version — e.g. "[^47]: Calculated: `ROIC = NOPAT / invested capital` = 0.1562... (`aer.calc.ratios:return_on_invested_capital`, code version `6d9c6c80d78a`)". A's figures rest on bare URLs with no hash and, in one material case, on a secondary aggregator.

**A measured account of its own citation integrity.** The Validation Metrics table reports citation_accuracy 1.00, hallucinated_citation_rate 0, primary_source_ratio 1.00, temporal_compliance 1.00, source_coverage 0.94 against stated thresholds, plus a "Point-in-time: enforced" stamp and "Non-binding view: no view reached" in the header.

**An adversarial critique of its own thesis, printed.** Nine red-team findings by section and severity, e.g. "Red team — profitability, severity 5/5: Every headline margin in the draft is contradicted by the recorded calculations," and "Red team — valuation, severity 4/5: There is no valuation content in this thesis at all... an investment case that cannot say what is priced in is not a case a reader can act on." A's §18 audits *sources*; B's audits its own argument. (A reader who follows the footnotes can see most of these objections are period-mismatched — [^107], [^108], [^110] and [^113] are FY2021 calculations and [^109] is FY2022, compared against FY2025 claims — but the document ships with all nine "Escalated for human decision at approval.")

**Definition-sensitivity discipline, stated repeatedly.** Historical Financial Analysis: ROIC is "built from NOPAT of $11,339m over invested capital of $72,578m... the denominators are closing balance-sheet amounts, not opening-and-closing averages. A definition that averaged the capital base... would yield a lower return on the same profit... A reader working on that stricter basis should treat the quoted return as the upper end of a range." Balance Sheet: "conventions that capitalise lease liabilities of $1.4bn, bring in pension and other financing obligations, or measure cover on gross finance expense... would show leverage appreciably higher." A quotes single-basis ratios without this.

**Falsification named to a specific document.** The Supporting Pillars table gives each proposition its arbiter: "The arbiter is the therapy area review, the revenue note and the segment information incorporated by reference into the Form 20-F dated February 24, 2026, read against the equivalent lines in the next annual filing. Product-level erosion that launch sales do not offset falsifies it."

**Structural refusal where evidence is absent**, with the gate quoted: Catalysts carries "Insufficient evidence: This section's policy requires 1 distinct source(s); its claims cite 0"; Comparable companies states "every one of the eight proposed peers was excluded, because this research holds no filings and no price series for it"; a Scope and limitations section collects the refusals.

**Primary-sourced FY2025 balance sheet and cash flow detail A does not have.** Total assets $114,074m, accounts payable $25,280m, lease liabilities $1,421m, short-term investments $30m, H1 2025 cash flow lines (investing −$3,361m, financing −$2,189m, dividends $3,357m), FY2025 debt proceeds $15m against repayments $2,029m, "no share repurchases have been made since 2012", and the 20-F's EBT/Alexion replacement-award cash-flow classification policies. A's 30 June 2026 balance sheet table is sourced to "[Dukascopy summary]... a secondary source".

**Two points of substance A never raises.** Segment Analysis: AstraZeneca "discloses only a single reportable operating segment" and "explicitly does not monitor profitability by individual product, brand or drug class" — the structural reason product-level analysis is hard. Earnings Quality: the Fusion development-stage intangibles "fair valued using a multi-period excess earnings method, with key assumptions for probability of technical and regulatory success, peak-year sales and revenue erosion," one programme "terminated and written off in full in December 2024, only months after the business was consolidated from June 2024."

**A recorded source conflict with its tie-break logic:** "GSPC.INDX close on 2026-09-11... report 7656.98 against 7672.540000. There is nothing left to prefer one by."

**Five years of margin history** (gross 66.8% / 72.1% / 82.0% / 81.1% / 81.9% FY2021–25 in [^55]–[^59]) versus A's three-year record.
verdict.which_would_you_hand_to_a_colleague_and_:
**Document A**, with warnings.

It is the only one of the two that answers the brief. On expiry exposure it gives a number and shows its working (Farxiga "$8,492m global, = 14.5% of FY2025 Total Revenue", plus a revealed-erosion cross-check of "about 2.9 percentage points of group growth"). On oncology it separates cash already booked from cash assumed (Datroway's "$2m of FY2025 Product Sales and $77m of Alliance Revenue" against "more than twenty high-value readouts due over the next 18 months"), and the oncology-CAGR-to-$80bn grid states precisely how much assumption the 2030 ambition needs. On the balance sheet it puts the dividend and R&D against one cash flow in the §11 sources-and-uses table and reaches a conclusion — dividends are 34.1% of OCF and covered 2.86x on Core EPS, but net debt still rose $3,538m in H1 2026 "primarily due to dividend payments and deal-related expenses", so the marginal claim on the balance sheet is deal spend, not the dividend. It is current to 10 September 2026, and it has one genuinely original analytical contribution — that Core EPS excludes the amortisation of acquired IP while roughly $4bn a year of cash to acquire that IP recurs, with the reverse DCF showing what the market must instead believe (Ke 7.20%, g 3.90%, or a 30.8% terminal OCF margin against 24.8% delivered).

The warnings I would attach: the file opens with a stray working line ("I'll research AstraZeneca's primary sources before writing. Let me begin.") before the title; the entire 30 June 2026 balance sheet in §9 comes from a secondary aggregator the note elsewhere proves wrong about market cap; the 8.5% cost of equity is admitted to be "an assumption, not a derivation" and the note itself concedes "The rating is one assumption deep"; governance (§6) and comparables (§14.4) are empty by the author's own admission; and the headline "approximately 15% of revenue (Farxiga) is directly exposed" is a *global* figure for a *US* loss of exclusivity — A flags "US portion not separately sourced," but the answer sentence still carries the larger number.

Document B I would hand over only as an evidence-integrity exhibit, not as a research note. It answers none of the three focus questions — its own red team says so: "The load-bearing question is therefore posed but left entirely unevidenced." Its financial base "close[s] on 31 December 2025 and the latest interim period is Q2 2025 — several quarters behind this note's September 2026 as-of date", so the 12-month horizon is unaddressed. And as a document handed to a reader it defeats itself in three ways beyond the staleness: nine central claims are marked "Escalated for human decision at approval" with no resolution; the two tables that carry the most citations ("Segment mix", 18 footnotes; "Revenue and margin history", 21 footnotes) are absent — "*Rendered in the HTML and PDF editions of this report*" — so the cited figures are not in the file; and it contradicts itself on whether comparatives exist, asserting "with no prior-year comparatives no growth rate is asserted" and "There is no comparable prior-year column" directly above and below a table showing revenue from FY2021 to FY2025, from which the +8.6% it declines to state is one division away. Smaller unforced errors compound it: EPS is $6.54 diluted in "At a glance" but "basic earnings of $6.60 per share" in Growth Outlook, unreconciled; and "Two dividend rates are recorded for the period: 1.03 dollars per share and 2.10 dollars per share" mixes an interim from one year with a second interim from another, implying an annual rate that is wrong.

What I would take from B into A is its apparatus, not its content: the artefact hashes and source tiers, the formula-and-code-version record behind each ratio, the definition-sensitivity paragraphs on ROIC and leverage, and the habit of naming the exact filing that would falsify each proposition. A note with A's substance and B's provenance discipline would be better than either.

verdict.what_A_has_that_B_lacks:
Substance on all three focus questions, and arithmetic I could re-perform from the page.

Q1 (patent expiry): A's "The patent-cliff question" table names each crystallised LOE with a figure and a source — Farxiga "$8,492m global, = 14.5% of FY2025 Total Revenue", Brilinta "decreased by 38% ... driven by generic entry in the US and Europe in the first half of 2025", Soliris US "−28% to $1,092m", plus the quoted off-patent list (Crestor, Nexium, Pulmicort, Seloken, Synagis, Zoladex) — then adds a revealed-exposure measure (CVRM $12,764m + V&IT $846m = 23.2% of revenue; −12% and −26% CER run-rates ≈ $1.75bn ≈ "2.9 percentage points of group growth"). B quantifies none of this and names no product.

Q2 (oncology): A separates delivered from assumed. Delivered: Note 2 product lines with two-year CAGRs (Imfinzi +22.8%, Calquence +18.3%, Truqap $6m→$728m), Enhertu combined $4,982m of which AZ books "55.7% (computed)", named approvals (Datroway June 2025, Baxfendy US in H1 2026), and a growth decomposition — "Oncology contributed approximately +6.9 percentage points ... BioPharmaceuticals subtracted approximately 1.8 points". Assumed: the §13 grid showing "Only at a sustained ~14% oncology CAGR does the rest of the group get to be flat". It also explicitly refuses a third-party number — tozorakimab "peak sales exceeding $5 billion" is "a third-party projection ... I do not use it in my forecasts".

Q3 (dividend + R&D): cover 2.86x Core / 2.06x Reported, dividends "34.1% of FY2025 OCF", R&D at 23.5% of revenue, a FY2025 sources-and-uses table that reconciles to within $702m of the actual net-debt move and says so, the net-debt walk 23,374 → 26,912 in six months, and a verdict: "The constraint on AstraZeneca is not solvency; it is that the business consumes cash faster than Core EPS suggests."

Also: H1 2026 results entirely (revenue $30,672m, OCF $6,224m vs $7,099m, cash tax at 31% of reported PBT), FY2026 guidance, the 9 July 2026 CARDIO-TTRansform failure, the 2 February 2026 NYSE/ADR restructuring, a price and a share count, a full DCF with all twelve assumptions tabulated with sources, a reverse DCF (7.20% Ke / 3.90% g / 30.8% terminal OCF margin), three numbered scenarios, two 30-cell sensitivity grids, a catalyst calendar, a consensus comparison ($212.54) with the bridge to its own $132, and a 21-item validation log. I checked roughly 25 of A's computations (market cap, EV multiples, the 6.38% CAGR, growth attribution, every DCF row, terminal value, the 58% TV share, the probability weighting, the −15.2% total return) and they all tie.
verdict.what_B_has_that_A_lacks:
Provenance machinery, and primary-source purity.

Every figure in B carries either a T1_REGULATORY footnote with publisher, publication date, retrieval date, tier and an artefact hash (the Sources table lists `f8ee3de56da6`, `5f65a1e4d20e`, etc.), or a named calculation with formula, module and code version — e.g. "[^78]: `interest cover = operating income / interest expense` = 8.1128 ... (`aer.calc.ratios:interest_cover`, code version `6d9c6c80d78a`)". No secondary source appears anywhere; A by contrast sources its whole 30 June 2026 balance-sheet table, its current ratio of 0.89x, its negative working capital of $3,588m and its 15.9x interest cover to Dukascopy, and its reference price to CNN/Robinhood.

Three dated primary items A reaches only through news digests or not at all: the Etcamah US approval in HR+ breast cancer and the Imfinzi+Imdelltra SCLC overall-survival readout (both 8 September 2026, cited to SEC URLs; A cites the 8 September item to "Robinhood news digest" and "stockanalysis digest"), and the "ADMISSION TO TRADING - EUR2.55 BILLION BOND OFFERING" of 1 September 2026 — direct evidence on the funding question that A does not have.

A published adversarial audit: nine red-team findings with severities and a validator scorecard against thresholds ("Red team — profitability, severity 5/5", citation_accuracy 1.00, primary_source_ratio 1.00), each "Escalated for human decision at approval" — the reader is told where the document's own referees disagree with it.

Two pieces of discipline A abandons. B names the manoeuvre it refuses — "apportioning worldwide product revenue by a group-level regional ratio would manufacture a figure not actually reported and is avoided here" — and it declines a DCF rather than discount at a guessed rate, whereas A concedes "Cost of equity: 8.5% — an assumption, not a derivation" and then prints a rating and a target on it. B is also better on definitional humility for leverage: conventions capitalising leases or measuring cover on gross finance expense "would show leverage appreciably higher and coverage appreciably thinner". And B carries FY2021–FY2025 revenue with each year's computed margin; A has three years only.
verdict.which_would_you_hand_to_a_colleague_and_:
A, with three written warnings attached.

A is the only one of the two that answers the brief. B's own text disqualifies it from Q1 ("the underlying patent expiry dates, US regulatory exclusivity periods, and ex-US supplementary protection certificate or data-exclusivity dates ... were not present in the material reviewed"), from Q2 ("Asset-level late-stage disclosure ... is not available ... The judgements below therefore rest on financial structure rather than on named assets"), and largely from Q3, where its financial record "close[s] on 31 December 2025 and the latest interim period is Q2 2025 — several quarters behind this note's September 2026 as-of date". A note dated 11 September 2026 that never sees H1 2026 cannot say whether a balance sheet supports anything "through the horizon". B is a well-built provenance artefact and a poor research note.

Worse for B, its numbers fight each other. "Key Points" says "no invested-capital, cost-of-capital or return-on-invested-capital figure is on record"; the Investment Thesis and Growth Outlook then both quote "a return on invested capital of 15.6%" and infer that reinvestment "has so far cleared a plausible cost of capital". "Key Points" warns that reading the gross line "as room to fund launch spending without operating-margin consequence is the error to avoid"; Growth Outlook then says the gross margin "leaves unusually wide room to fund commercial launch spending without compressing the operating line". It asserts "no prior-period comparatives ... are on record" while printing FY2021–FY2025 revenue at the top of page one and FY2021–FY2025 margins in footnotes 55–69. It kills the DCF because "the filings carry none — neither diluted, basic nor a plain outstanding figure" of share count, while printing diluted EPS of $6.54 against net income of $10,225m, which implies one. And its own red team says the profitability core is "unevidenced" (severity 5/5: claimed 81.9%/23.4%/17.4% against register values 0.668/0.028/0.003) — findings that on inspection are themselves partly wrong, since footnotes 55–69 show those register values belong to FY2021 and FY2022 and footnote 80 does record the 0.9381 current ratio the red team says is absent. Either reading is bad: the document either prints figures its register contradicts, or ships an audit that cannot tell one fiscal year from another, and leaves the conflict unresolved for the reader.

The warnings on A. First, the rating is one unsourced number deep, and A says so: "If the correct cost of equity for this company today is 7.2% rather than 8.5%, the stock is fairly valued and the rating should be Hold." Second, the tables bearing on Q3 — current ratio, quick ratio, working capital, interest cover, and the entire 30 June 2026 balance sheet — come from Dukascopy, a source A elsewhere distrusts enough to discard its market cap, EV and P/E; the reference price is CNN, the consensus is stockanalysis.com, and the peer table is eleven rows of "not sourced". Third, A is visibly answering a neighbouring brief: its labelled questions are US drug pricing, the patent cliff, and whether oncology is in the price. So Q2 is answered obliquely, and Q3 is never posed as a question — the reader must assemble it from §9 and §11, and A never builds a forward funding bridge putting the $3.30 dividend and 23.5%-of-revenue R&D against projected cash. On Q1 A also concedes the part that matters most for terminal value: it could not extract the expiry schedule, and "I will not state dates I did not read." That refusal is to its credit, and it is still a hole.

Net: A gives a colleague something to attack — a thesis, a price, a bridge to consensus, and arithmetic that reconciles. B gives them an audit trail around an absence.

verdict.what_A_has_that_B_lacks:
Machine provenance B cannot match. Every source in A's "Sources" table carries a content hash (`f8ee3de56da6` for the XBRL facts, `5f65a1e4d20e` for the 20-F) and every derived number cites formula, value, module and code version (footnote 5: "`gross margin = gross profit / revenue` = 0.819 ... `aer.calc.ratios:gross_margin`, code version `4c63dbfc4794`"). B's numbers are re-derivable from stated inputs but nothing is content-addressed, so B cannot prove the filing it read is the filing still there.

A quantified integrity panel B has no analogue for: "Validation Metrics" (citation_accuracy 1.00, hallucinated_citation_rate 0, primary_source_ratio 1.00, temporal_compliance 1.00, source_coverage 0.9412) each against a stated threshold, plus a declared "Point-in-time: enforced" and a named look_ahead_recall metric.

An adversarial challenge to its own arithmetic. A's "Disagreements" carries eight severity-graded red-team findings against the draft's own headline numbers — "Red team — profitability, severity 5/5: Every headline profitability figure in the draft is contradicted by the run's own recorded calculations", and severity 5/5 on the balance sheet ("recorded interest_cover calculation is 0.812 and the recorded net_debt_to_ebitda is 3.223"). B red-teams third-party sources in Section 18 but never its own computations.

A longer margin history. A's footnotes 39–53 carry a FY2021–FY2025 series: gross margin 66.8% → 72.1% → 82.0% → 81.1% → 81.9%, operating margin 2.8% → 8.5% → 17.9% → 18.5% → 23.4%, net margin 0.3% → 7.4% → 13.0% → 13.0% → 17.4%. B's "Three-year record" starts at FY2023, so the Alexion-era distortion and the scale of the margin rebuild are invisible in B.

Balance-sheet definitional discipline. A's "Balance Sheet & Liquidity" sets the derived net debt of $23,911m against "The company's own net debt measure, loans and borrowings net of cash, other investments and derivative financial instruments ... a different and lower figure", and warns "leverage quoted from different sources should be checked against the definition behind it." B takes the company's $26,912m at face value. A also has the committed facilities "carrying no financial covenants", the bond maturity spread "from the late 2020s into the early 2030s" with hedge designations, the multi-year ERP programme as a continuing cash absorber, and the EBT/Alexion replacement-award classification policy.

A primary-source discount-rate anchor that B says does not exist. A's valuation commentary: "the Group states a post-tax weighted average cost of capital for its own impairment work and applies risk-adjusted post-tax rates to intangible assets whose upper end sits above it." B's Section 18 item 19 lists risk-free rate, ERP and beta as unsourced and calls its 8.5% "the weakest link".

Two terminal methods carried side by side with the share of value each asserts (87.2% Gordon, 76.0% exit multiple) and a caveat that names the direction of its own bias: "the equity weight is understated, the debt weight overstated, and the resulting WACC too low. Every valuation discounted at it is correspondingly too high."

A "Prior Research Comparison" that tests the previous run's confirmed assumptions against what has since become checkable ("Not yet observable: no full fiscal year after 11 September 2026 is in the store"), and an explicit "Scope and limitations" list naming which sections failed their evidence policy. Also the Fusion point: "An in-development intangible recognised on the Fusion acquisition, consolidated from 4 June 2024, was impaired in full in December 2024" — a within-months write-off B does not surface, and A's licensed-data redistribution determination has no counterpart in B.
verdict.what_B_has_that_A_lacks:
Answers to all three focus questions, sized. On expiries, "The patent-cliff question (part 2 of 3 posed in the brief)" gives Farxiga $8,492m = 14.5% of FY2025 revenue with US LOE already begun, Brilinta −38% on US/EU generic entry, Soliris US −28% to $1,092m on biosimilar pressure, the off-patent legacy list, then a revealed-exposure cross-check: CVRM $12,764m plus V&IT $846m = 23.2% of revenue, running at −12% and −26% CER in H1 2026, "about 2.9 percentage points of group growth absorbed each year". A's "Segment Analysis" instead carries "Insufficient evidence", correctly identifies that it needs "Note 2 (Revenue) or Note 7 (Segment information)", and stops; its Key Points say "Exclusivity exposure — unresolved."

Product-level revenue at all. B has the five largest products (Farxiga $8,492m, Tagrisso $7,254m, Imfinzi $6,063m, Ultomiris $4,718m, Calquence $3,518m), the FY2025 therapy-area table with CER growth, and a Note 2 oncology-by-region table with computed two-year CAGRs (Imfinzi +22.8%, Calquence +18.3%, Truqap $6m → $728m). A names no product except "HR-positive breast cancer".

A real separation of delivered from assumed oncology growth. "The oncology question (part 3 of 3)" shows oncology at 46% of H1 2026 revenue growing 15% CER, weights it to "+6.9 percentage points" of group growth against BioPharmaceuticals' "−1.8 points", concludes "oncology accounted for more than the entirety of group growth in the half", then tests the assumed part: a table showing "Only at a sustained ~14% oncology CAGR does the rest of the group get to be flat." It also quarantines a third-party number: tozorakimab "peak sales exceeding $5 billion — that is a third-party projection, not a company figure, and I do not use it in my forecasts." A's Growth Outlook carries "the pipeline is carried at zero contribution rather than at an assumed one" — methodologically clean, but it tells a reader nothing about the pipeline.

The dividend/R&D/BD question answered jointly. Section 10's three owner-cash definitions (OCF $14,575m; less capex $11,305m; less non-capex investing $7,350m), Section 11's cover (2.86x Core, 2.06x Reported, dividends 34.1% of OCF) and decelerating dividend (+7%, +3%, +3.1% implied), and the verdict: "The constraint on AstraZeneca is not solvency; it is that the business consumes cash faster than Core EPS suggests, so incremental deals are increasingly debt-funded — as H1 2026's $3,538m net-debt build demonstrates."

Anything after 31 December 2025. H1 2026 revenue $30,672m, Q2 2026 CER +5%, OCF down $875m to $6,224m with the margin falling 25.3% → 20.3%, FY2026 guidance reconfirmed 27 July 2026, the $80bn 2030 ambition and its 6.38% CAGR, the 9 July 2026 CARDIO-TTRansform failure and ~9–10% one-day fall, generic dapagliflozin marketed by August 2026, and the 2 February 2026 NYSE ordinary-share listing with the ADR facility closed — with its practical consequence spelt out for a US holder. A states "no FY2026 interim results are available, so this picture may be stale as of September 2026" and compares its December 2025 balance sheet with June **2025**.

A decision. Price $159.64, market cap $247,596m, EV $274,508m, a full multiple set, target $132, UNDERWEIGHT, −15.2% total return. A records "Non-binding view: no view reached" and carries no share price anywhere, so its $169.80 and $333.48 outputs cannot be compared to anything.

A usable model. FCFE = OCF − capex − BD with ten forecast years printed line by line, twelve numbered assumptions each justified and sourced, terminal value 58% of total, a reverse-DCF ("the market is paying for ... a cost of equity of 7.20% ... or a 3.90% perpetual growth rate ... or a sustained operating cash-flow margin of 30.8%"), two 30-cell sensitivity grids, and three scenarios with every input changed and probabilities assigned.

Earnings-quality work A does not reach: the $4,735m Core-to-Reported bridge and its three-year gap series, the Collaboration Revenue $923m → $99m washout read as a quality improvement worth a 1.5pp headwind, royalty buyouts expensed in cost of sales ($170m BMS, $65m Compugen) credited as conservative, and the cash-tax anomaly — "31% of Reported profit before tax, against a Reported effective rate of 17% ... the single item in the accounts I would most want management to explain."

Catalysts and outside view. Nine dated or near-dated catalysts with what each would settle; A's "Catalysts" section is empty under "Insufficient evidence". B also confronts consensus ($212.54, HSBC Hold, Berenberg and RBC Buy) and decomposes its own difference into dollars per share (~$22 for the BD charge, ~$33 for the cost of equity). B's partner-economics point — AZ books 55.7% of combined Enhertu sales of $4,982m — has no counterpart in A.
verdict.which_would_you_hand_to_a_colleague_and_:
B, with two caveats attached in writing.

B is the only one of the two that answers the brief. It sizes the expiry exposure (≈15% of revenue in Farxiga's already-begun US LOE, ≈23% sitting in two therapy areas currently declining at −12% and −26% CER), it separates oncology's delivered contribution from the assumed part (+6.9pp of H1 growth delivered; the $80bn ambition needing a ~14% oncology CAGR before the rest of the group can even be flat), and it answers the dividend-plus-R&D question on the right basis — cash after capex *and* after the ~$4bn a year of business development — landing on "not solvency ... the business consumes cash faster than Core EPS suggests". It is current to within six weeks of the as-of date, it prices the stock, and it states what would make it wrong in a way I could act on or argue with: "A reader who takes either view reaches fair value at or above spot", and "The rating is one assumption deep."

The caveats I would flag. First, B's entire 30 June 2026 balance-sheet table, its 15.9x interest cover and its −$3,588m working capital come from Dukascopy, a secondary source the same note elsewhere discredits ("I use Dukascopy only for its balance-sheet line items ... and I discard its market-cap, EV and P/E figures") — that is a reasonable rule, but it means the Q3 answer rests partly on unverified numbers, and only net debt and the ratings are primary. Second, B headlines Farxiga's whole $8,492m as "approximately 15% of revenue ... directly exposed" while admitting in the same row that the "US portion not separately sourced"; the exposure to a *US* LOE is smaller than 15%, and the headline overstates it.

A is not a substitute. Its provenance machinery is the better artefact — hashed sources, formula-and-code-version citations, a validation panel, an adversarial log — and I would keep it for the FY2021–25 margin series, the two-definitions warning on net debt, the covenant-free facility and maturity-spread detail, and the company's own impairment WACC as a discount-rate anchor. But it declares two of the three questions "unresolved", carries no catalysts, no comparables, no price and "no view reached", and its DCF is not usable: it admits the book-weight WACC of 5.8% makes "Every valuation discounted at it ... correspondingly too high", 76–87% of value is terminal, and its commentary claims the forecast inputs are not "exotic relative to what the company actually printed" when revenue growth of 11.9% is roughly twice what management guides and the 14.2% EBIT margin is well below the 23.4% printed. Worst for someone acting with their own money, A's own red team records at severity 5/5 that the interest cover and leverage answering focus question 3 may be inverted (0.812x cover, 3.22x net debt/EBITDA against the claimed 8.11x and 1.27x), and all eight disagreements are left "Escalated for human decision at approval" — unresolved on the page. The footnotes suggest the red team compared FY2025 claims against FY2021/FY2022 calculations (footnote 143 is interest cover "for FY2021"), so the challenge is probably the thing that is wrong — but the document does not say so, and its Executive Summary separately contradicts its own body, denying that any "invested capital, return on invested capital, share price or share count is available" while the thesis quotes ROIC of 15.6% on $72.6bn of invested capital. I would not open or add to a position on a document that flags its own headline solvency numbers as possibly reversed and then leaves it there.

verdict.what_A_has_that_B_lacks:
A has a provenance *mechanism* B never attempts. Every computed figure in A resolves to a formula, a period and a code version — footnote 57 reads "Calculated: `interest cover = operating income / interest expense` = 8.1128 ... for FY2025 (`aer.calc.ratios:interest_cover`, code version `4c63dbfc4794`)" — and the Sources table gives each artefact a hash (`f8ee3de56da6`, `5f65a1e4d20e`). Nothing in B ties a number to a named formula or a content hash. A also labels who chose each valuation input: the Cost of Capital and Forecast Assumptions tables distinguish "set by the operator and confirmed at the assumptions gate" from "proposed by aer.services.assumption_proposals ... and confirmed by the operator".

A's self-audit of its own DCF is better than B's. "Recorded Caveats" states that book equity was used as the equity weight, so "the equity weight is understated, the debt weight overstated, and the resulting WACC too low. Every valuation discounted at it is correspondingly too high"; that "More than three quarters of the enterprise value is terminal value"; and that "The bridge from enterprise value to equity value is net debt alone. Associate holdings, minority interests and pension deficits are not read off the filings by this build."

Four analytical points in A have no counterpart in B. (1) Valuation Commentary: "R&D of $14.2 billion on revenue of $58.7 billion is expensed inside the EBIT margin, so the model pays in full for the pipeline each year while crediting it only through the growth rate." (2) The same section: "A single revenue growth path cannot simultaneously represent decline in marketed products as exclusivity lapses and replacement of that revenue by pipeline assets; the two are netted into one rate" — a flaw B's own model has and does not name. (3) Balance Sheet & Liquidity flags the net-debt definition trap: "The company's own net debt measure ... is a different and lower figure ... The two definitions are not interchangeable, and leverage quoted from different sources should be checked against the definition behind it." (4) Earnings Quality: "An in-development intangible recognised on the Fusion acquisition, consolidated from 4 June 2024, was impaired in full in December 2024 after the related activities were terminated — a write-off within months of the acquisition-date valuation." A also insists on the EBITDA-vs-post-amortisation distinction — "a reader who prefers a cover ratio struck on operating income of $13,743m ... will reach a materially lower figure" — where B quotes an unexamined 15.9x interest cover from a secondary source.

Finally, A refuses to fabricate rather than estimating: Segment Analysis says "Presenting such a table without the underlying disclosure would substitute assertion for measurement, which this note avoids", and A carries a Validation Metrics table with named thresholds (citation_accuracy, primary_source_ratio, temporal_compliance) and an eight-item red-team log that B has no analogue for.
verdict.what_B_has_that_A_lacks:
B has the last twelve months of the company. A's newest financial data is FY2025 (year to 31 December 2025) compared against "Q2 FY2025" (30 June 2025); A admits it in Key Risks — "Figures stop at the year ended December 2025; no FY2026 interim results are available, so this picture may be stale as of September 2026." B carries H1 2026 (Total Revenue $30,672m, +6% CER, Core EPS $5.21, OCF $6,224m, net debt $26,912m, A1/A+ ratings), FY2026 guidance reconfirmed 27 July 2026, the 9 July 2026 CARDIO-TTRansform failure and the 9–10% share fall, FDA-approved generic dapagliflozin (Aug 2026), and a close of $159.64 on 10 September 2026.

B has the product- and region-level revenue A says does not exist. Section 4.2 reproduces Note 2 of the 20-F by medicine and region (Tagrisso $7,254m, Imfinzi $6,063m, Calquence $3,518m, Lynparza $3,279m) with two-year CAGRs; Section 4.1 gives the five therapy areas and reconciles them ($54,601m disclosed against $55,573m Product Sales, "$972m residual"). A's Segment Analysis is an empty section stamped "Insufficient evidence".

B has a price, a rating and a target: "Reference price: $159.64 ... 12-month target: $132 ... Rating: UNDERWEIGHT", decomposed as "−17.3% capital return and −15.2% total return including the intended $3.30 FY2026 dividend". A prints no share price at all — I grepped; there is none — so its outputs of $169.80 and $333.48 cannot be compared to anything, and its header says "Non-binding view: no view reached".

B has a reverse DCF that states what the market must believe — "a cost of equity of 7.20% (at 2.0% terminal growth), or a 3.90% perpetual growth rate (at my 8.5% cost of equity), or a sustained operating cash-flow margin of 30.8% of revenue against 24.8% delivered in FY2025" — and two 30-cell sensitivity grids printed in the text ("Only 6 of 30 cells reach or exceed the current price"). A's heatmap is absent: "*Rendered in the HTML and PDF editions of this report.*"

B has numeric scenarios where every input moves (bear/base/bull 2030 revenue $67,186m / $78,949m / $84,707m → $70.72 / $126.98 / $203.48, weighted 25/50/25 to $132.04). A's "Scenarios" table moves nothing — it lists FY2025 actuals nine times.

B reconciles to consensus and attributes the gap: "$212.54, described as +33.40% above the latest price", then "My target is 38% below the reported consensus. Where the difference comes from, precisely" — business development treated as a cost (~$22/share), cost of equity (~$33/share), terminal growth, revenue path.

B's arithmetic is reproducible on a calculator because the inputs are printed inline: "16.4x trailing-twelve-month Core EPS of $9.71 (computed: $9.16 − $4.66 + $5.21)". I re-derived roughly thirty of B's computed figures — market cap, EV, all the multiples, the 6.38% CAGR to $80bn, the 78.9% OCF-to-Core-EBIT conversion, the whole ten-year FCFE table, the terminal value, the $126.98 per share, the $132.04 weighting — and they hold.

B triages its own sources. Section 18 lists seven cross-checks that passed and seven inconsistencies with resolutions, including "Dukascopy's enterprise value is wrong ... I use Dukascopy only for its balance-sheet line items ... and I discard its market-cap, EV and P/E figures" and the GuruFocus FCF reconciliation. B also dates its catalysts (Dizal close H2 2026, oral PCSK9 data H1 2027, Q3 results). A's Catalysts section is empty: "its claims cite 0".
verdict.which_would_you_hand_to_a_colleague_and_:
B — with two warnings attached, but B nonetheless.

The decisive point is that I cannot trust a single headline number in A on A's own account. Its "Validation & Disagreements" section contains eight findings, five of them severity 4 or 5, alleging that A's own recorded calculations contradict its text: "The draft asserts gross margin 81.9%, operating margin 23.4%, net margin 17.4%, EBITDA margin 32.1% and ROE 21.0%. The only recorded calculations carrying those names return gross margin 0.668 and 0.721 ... No recorded calculation reproduces any draft figure"; "The recorded interest_cover calculation is 0.812 and the recorded net_debt_to_ebitda is 3.223 ... On the recorded numbers, earnings do not cover interest and leverage is not modest"; "The only recorded return_on_invested_capital is 0.0823 ... against the claimed $72.6bn". The resolution given for all eight is the same non-answer: "Escalated for human decision at approval." Chasing footnotes 143, 145, 146 and 148 shows those "contradicting" calculations are FY2021 and FY2022 figures — so the red team compared across periods and A's FY2025 numbers are probably fine — but the disagreement prose never says so, and for the rest (net debt $24,452m vs $23,911m, debt-to-equity 0.783 vs 0.61, EBITDA $7,586m/$9,237m vs $18,829m, NOPAT $4.95bn vs $11.3bn) no citation resolves the period at all. Those are exactly the figures focus question 3 turns on. A reader handed the file cannot tell whether interest cover is 8.11x or 0.81x.

A is also self-contradictory outside that log. The Executive Summary states "No discount rate, terminal growth assumption, invested capital, return on invested capital, share price or share count is available" — and the Valuation section then prints a WACC of 5.8%, terminal growth of 2.5%, invested capital of $72,578m, ROIC of 15.6% and 1,562,000,000 shares. Beta is 0.4 in the Cost of Capital table and "Confirmed at 0.3" in Prior Research Comparison; capex intensity is 0.033377 in one table and "Confirmed at 0.05" in the other. Historical Financial Analysis insists "The reported annual history we can stand behind ... covers the year ended 31 December 2025 only" while "At a glance" prints revenue for FY2021 through FY2025. On question 3 A answers twice and oppositely: Cash Flow Analysis says "free cash flow covered the dividend with room to spare" and describes "a business funding its capital programme and a large, growing-by-policy dividend entirely from internally generated cash", while Growth Outlook says "Treat balance-sheet capacity to sustain R&D and business development as an open question, not a settled strength." Neither reconciles the other. And on the header's "no view reached", Investment Thesis says "we hold a constructive but low-confidence view".

On the three focus questions B answers and A declines. Q1: B gives "approximately 15% of revenue (Farxiga) is directly exposed to an LOE that has already begun inside the horizon, and approximately 23% of revenue sits in the two therapy areas currently in decline", sizes the drag at "about 2.9 percentage points of group growth absorbed each year", and states its limit honestly — "I could not extract the per-product expiry years from that document ... I will not state dates I did not read". A's answer is "Exclusivity exposure — unresolved ... the available filings carry no product, molecule or geographic revenue split and no expiry dates". Q2: B separates earning approvals (Datroway US June 2025, Baxfendy US H1 2026, Saphnelo EU December 2025, Truqap $6m→$728m) from assumption (">20 high-value readouts" and the grid showing "Only at a sustained ~14% oncology CAGR does the rest of the group get to be flat"). A carries "the pipeline ... at zero contribution rather than at an assumed one" — defensible, but not an answer. Q3: B gives dividend cover of 2.86x Core and 2.06x Reported, dividends at "34.1% of FY2025 OCF", dividend growth decelerating "+7% (FY2024), +3% (FY2025), +3.1% implied (FY2026)", R&D at 23.5% of revenue, BD at ~$4bn a year, and the conclusion "the constraint on AstraZeneca is not solvency; it is that the business consumes cash faster than Core EPS suggests, so incremental deals are increasingly debt-funded — as H1 2026's $3,538m net-debt build demonstrates."

The two warnings I would attach. First, B's balance sheet at 30 June 2026 — the table feeding net debt/equity of 0.534x, the "117% of total equity" goodwill point and the 15.9x interest cover — comes from Dukascopy, a secondary source whose market-cap and P/E figures B itself demonstrates are wrong; B discloses this ("a secondary source; see Section 18 for my reservations about it") but the answer to question 3 partly rests on it. Second, B's own summary of its fragility is accurate and should be read first: "If the correct cost of equity for this company today is 7.2% rather than 8.5%, the stock is fairly valued and the rating should be Hold ... The rating is one assumption deep." I would also hand over A's Valuation Commentary paragraph on the blended growth rate, because it identifies a flaw in B's model that B does not see.

verdict.what_A_has_that_B_lacks:
Per-figure provenance machinery. Every computed number in A carries a formula and a code version (e.g. [^57] "`interest cover = operating income / interest expense` = 8.1128 ... code version `4c63dbfc4794`"), and every fact carries publisher, publication date, retrieval date, tier and an artefact hash (Sources table: `f8ee3de56da6`, `5f65a1e4d20e`). B has nothing equivalent — its computations show inputs but no formula registry.

Per-assumption audit trail. A's "Cost of Capital" and "Forecast Assumptions" tables mark each input as either "set by the operator and confirmed at the assumptions gate" (risk-free 4.8%, beta 0.4, ERP 0.045) or "proposed by aer.services.assumption_proposals with a stated justification, and confirmed by the operator". B's assumptions are self-chosen; nobody signed them off.

Self-refutation of its own valuation. A's "Recorded Caveats" says book equity was used as the equity weight so "the equity weight is understated, the debt weight overstated, and the resulting WACC too low. Every valuation discounted at it is correspondingly too high" — it discredits its own $169.80/$333.48 outputs. B has no comparable act of self-demolition.

Two terminal methods carried in parallel with the spread presented as the answer's width: "The two terminal methods disagree by more than a quarter. That is information, not an error", with terminal-value share disclosed at 87.2% (Gordon) and 76% (exit multiple).

An adversarial-review record published in the document. "Validation & Disagreements" prints eight red-team findings at severity 3-5 against its own draft, plus a validation metric table (citation_accuracy 1.00, hallucinated_citation_rate 0, primary_source_ratio 1.00, temporal_compliance 1.00).

A five-year margin series (footnotes [^39]-[^53]: gross margin 66.8% FY2021 rising to 82.0% FY2025; operating margin 2.8% to 23.4%) — more history than B's three years, though it sits only in footnotes.

The clean statement that a coverage ratio struck after amortisation "is distinctly thinner than the headline suggests", and that the company's own net-debt definition ("loans and borrowings net of cash, other investments and derivative financial instruments") is "a different and lower figure" than the derived $23,911m.
verdict.what_B_has_that_A_lacks:
Answers to focus questions 1 and 2, which A marks "unresolved". §4.1 gives FY2025/FY2024 therapy-area Product Sales (Oncology 23,698/20,275, CVRM 12,764, R&I 8,167, V&IT 846, Rare Disease 9,126) from the 20-F Annual Report extract; §4.2 gives medicine-level oncology revenue by region for FY2023-25 with computed CAGRs (Tagrisso 7,254/+11.8%, Imfinzi 6,063/+22.8%, Calquence 3,518/+18.3%, Truqap $6m to $728m). A's "Segment Analysis" carries a banner — "Insufficient evidence: This section's policy requires at least one primary source (tier 1 or 2); none of its cited evidence is primary" — and states no product-level figure anywhere.

Sized patent exposure. §12 "The patent-cliff question": Farxiga "$8,492m global, = 14.5% of FY2025 Total Revenue", LOE already begun and named as an H1 2026 headwind in the 6-K; Brilinta "−38% ... driven by generic entry in the US and Europe in the first half of 2025"; Soliris US −28% to $1,092m on biosimilar pressure; plus a revealed cross-check — CVRM and Infectious Disease at 23.2% of revenue running −12% and −26% CER, "about 2.9 percentage points of group growth absorbed each year". A says only that exposure "cannot be separated" and "should be treated as present and material but unmeasured."

The approvals-versus-assumptions discrimination the brief asks for. §2 point 1 attributes +6.9pp of group CER growth to oncology against −1.8pp from BioPharmaceuticals, concluding "oncology accounted for more than the entirety of group growth in the half"; the §13 grid shows "Only at a sustained ~14% oncology CAGR does the rest of the group get to be flat" against the $80bn ambition. It names sourced approvals (Baxfendy US-approved H1 2026, Datroway June 2025 with $2m product sales and $77m alliance revenue) and refuses a third-party peak-sales number outright: "that is a third-party projection, not a company figure, and I do not use it in my forecasts."

Everything after 31 December 2025. H1 2026 revenue $30,672m (+6% CER, Q2 +5%), Core EPS $5.21, OCF $6,224m, net debt $26,912m at 30 June 2026, FY2026 guidance reconfirmed 27 July 2026, the 9 July 2026 CARDIO-TTRansform failure and the ~9-10% share fall, the 2 February 2026 NYSE ordinary-share listing harmonisation and ADR closure, FY2026 upfronts (CSPC $1,104m, Dizal $600m, Sino Bio $200m), China VBP. A's own Key Risks admit: "Figures stop at the year ended December 2025 ... so this picture may be stale as of September 2026."

The third claim on cash that A never quantifies. §10's three-definition table — OCF $14,575m, less capex $11,305m, less non-capex investing $3,955m = $7,350m — and the observation that in FY2024 "business development consumed more cash than capex did." A's Capital Allocation lists "Dividend payments, Capital expenditure, Debt repayment" and never sizes the ~$4bn/yr intangible and milestone spend, despite noting the $6,808m investing outflow.

A market price and therefore a conclusion: $159.64, market cap $247,596m, EV $274,508m, multiples on four bases, a reverse DCF solving for cost of equity 7.20%, terminal growth 3.90% or terminal OCF margin 30.8%, two printed sensitivity grids, probability-weighted scenarios with every input changed explicitly, and a rating. A's header reads "Non-binding view: no view reached" and its comparables section excludes all eight peers.

Dated catalysts (Dizal close H2 2026, oral PCSK9 data H1 2027, FY2026 results as "the cleanest test of the patent-cliff thesis") against A's Catalysts banner "its claims cite 0" sources. An external benchmark — consensus $212.54, HSBC Hold, Berenberg Buy — with the gap decomposed into ~$22/share for business-development treatment and ~$33/share for cost of equity; A's "Prior Research Comparison" only compares itself to its own prior run.
verdict.which_would_you_hand_to_a_colleague_and_:
B, with two caveats stapled to the front.

The brief asked three questions with a 12-month horizon. A answers one of them and does so on data that stops eight and a half months before the as-of date; its Executive Summary says so three times over — "Exclusivity exposure — unresolved", "Reverse DCF and pipeline — unresolved", "US pricing and tariffs — unresolved" — and its header records "no view reached". Declining to fabricate is the right instinct, but a note that cannot locate product-level revenue or a patent schedule for a company that publishes both (B links the FY2025 20-F Note 2 revenue tables and the "Patent Expiries of Key Marketed Products, as at 10 February 2026") has an acquisition problem, not an evidence problem. Six source documents, five of them one XBRL endpoint and a 20-F, is not a research base for this brief.

B earns its confident tone. I recomputed its load-bearing arithmetic and it holds: Farxiga 14.46% of revenue, CVRM+V&IT 23.17%, the 2.98pp annualised erosion, the 6.37% CAGR to $80bn, the +6.9/−1.8pp oncology attribution, 55.7% of combined Enhertu, market cap $247,596m, EV $274,508m, the terminal value $245,318m, $126.98 per share and the $132.04 probability weighting all reproduce. More importantly it separates delivered from assumed exactly where the brief asks — it refuses the tozorakimab "$5 billion" peak-sales figure because it is third-party, and it names its own weakest link twice ("Cost of equity: 8.5% — an assumption, not a derivation", "The rating is one assumption deep").

I did not prefer B on verifiability. A's provenance mechanism is better in kind. But A ships eight unresolved disagreements claiming its own recorded calculations contradict essentially every headline figure — "The only recorded calculations carrying those names return gross margin 0.668 and 0.721, operating margin 0.028 and 0.085 ... the profitability picture is unverified and may be materially overstated" — all "Escalated for human decision at approval" with no resolution. I traced the footnotes: [^143] is FY2021 interest cover, [^145] FY2021 gross margin, [^146] FY2021 free cash flow, [^148] FY2022 ROIC, so the red team compared across periods and the body is probably right. That took footnote forensics, not minutes, and no reader should have to do it. A also misdescribes its own ratio twice — Earnings Quality says "Interest cover of 8.11x relates EBITDA of $18,829m to interest expense of $1,694m" and "Coverage and leverage ratios cited here are EBITDA-based", when 18,829/1,694 is 11.1x and the cited formula is operating income over interest expense — and contradicts itself on which assumptions were used (DCF table: beta 0.4, capex intensity 0.033377; Prior Research Comparison: "beta ... Confirmed at 0.3", "capex intensity ... Confirmed at 0.05"). B's offsetting sins: the whole 30 June 2026 balance sheet in §9 comes from Dukascopy, a secondary source it elsewhere discredits; the $159.64 on which the entire rating hangs is a CNN quote cross-checked against Robinhood; "H1 2026 Core operating profit $10.5bn" is uncited; the FY2025 core opex table leaves $579m between its two expense lines and the stated total unexplained; and its "roughly 100-150bp" gross-margin haircut is an unsourced number doing real work in the valuation. Roughly matched failure modes.

The two caveats: B's §5 and §15 admit no primary source was read on most-favoured-nation pricing, Section 232 tariffs or Medicare maximum fair prices — "I have not estimated around that gap" — and §14.4 has no peer multiples at all, so the DCF has no cross-check. Both are disclosed in B's own words, which is why I would still hand it over. A's Growth Outlook holds the pipeline "at zero contribution", which is not a conservative answer to question 2; it is the absence of one.
